text: Which title did Benito Mussolini assume?
explanation: Benito Mussolini took the title 'Il Duce' (the Leader) as the Fascist dictator of Italy. Hitler's title was 'Fuhrer'.

subject: history
text: What was the 'Spartacus League'?
options: A Marxist revolutionary movement in Germany during the First World War
A communist movement in Italy during the First World War
A socialist revolutionary group in the United States during the Second World War
A liberal democratic movement in Russia during the Russian Revolution
explanation: The Spartacus League was a Marxist revolutionary group in Germany during World War I, led by Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht. It became the Communist Party of Germany.

subject: history
text: Who designed the flying shuttle?
explanation: John Kay invented the flying shuttle in 1733. It made weaving much faster, so demand for thread grew.

subject: history
text: In which session of the Indian National Congress was a resolution adopted to ‘urge the provincial committees to promote labour unions throughout India’?
explanation: In 1919 the Amritsar session of the Congress passed a resolution urging the provincial committees to promote labour unions throughout India, reflecting the rise of labour after World War I.

subject: history
text: Which of the following Acts abolished slavery in the British colonies?
explanation: The Slavery Abolition Act of 1833 abolished slavery in most of the British Empire (colonies). It followed a long campaign by abolitionists like William Wilberforce.

subject: history
text: The Indian National Congress split between moderates and extremists in its annual session in Surat in 1907. Who was the duly elected president of the session?
explanation: In the Surat session (1907), the Congress split into Moderates and Extremists. Rash Behari Ghose, a Moderate, was the elected President of the session.

subject: history
text: In which year was Watt's steam engine used for operating a spinning mill for the first time?
explanation: Watt's steam engine was first used to drive a cotton spinning mill in 1785, at Papplewick in Nottinghamshire, England. This was an important step in the mechanisation of textiles.

subject: history
text: Which of the following was NOT a reason for the Revolt of 1857 as mentioned in “The Azamgarh Proclamation”?
options: The British government, in making zamindari settlements, has imposed exorbitant Jumas.
The British government has monopolised the trade of all the fine and valuable merchandise.
The introduction of English articles into India have thrown the local artisans out of employ.
The natives employed in the civil and military services have high respect and high pay.
explanation: The Azamgarh Proclamation (1857) listed grievances like high land revenue, monopoly of trade and the ruin of local artisans by British goods. It did not say that Indians in service had high respect and pay. In fact they had low posts and pay.

subject: history
text: In which year was James Hargreaves' spinning jenny patented?
explanation: James Hargreaves invented the spinning jenny in 1764 and took out a patent for it in 1770. It let a worker spin many threads at once.

subject: history
text: In which year was Adam Smith's book Wealth of Nations published?
explanation: Adam Smith's 'The Wealth of Nations' was published in 1776, the same year as the American Declaration of Independence.

subject: history
text: The Tennis Court Oath is related to the:
explanation: The Tennis Court Oath (June 1789) was taken by members of the Third Estate in France. They swore not to disperse until France had a constitution. It belongs to the French Revolution.

subject: history
text: Who led the 1801 declaration of independence in Haiti, inspired by the ideals of the French Revolution?
explanation: Toussaint L'Ouverture, a former slave, led the Haitian revolution, which was inspired by the ideas of liberty and equality of the French Revolution. Haiti's constitution was declared in 1801.

subject: history
text: In Bareilly, the Revolt of 1857 was led by which of the following leaders?
explanation: Khan Bahadur Khan led the revolt of 1857 at Bareilly (Rohilkhand) and was proclaimed the Nawab. Kunwar Singh led in Bihar and Maulavi Ahmadullah in Faizabad.

subject: history
text: Which of the following industries was the centre of jute production in the world in the 18th century?
explanation: Dundee in Scotland was the world's centre of jute manufacturing in the 18th-19th centuries, using raw jute from India. Manchester and Lancashire were famous for cotton.

subject: history
text: Who accompanied Dr. BR Ambedkar to the first Round Table Conference in 1930 as a representative of the so-called Depressed Classes?
explanation: Rao Bahadur R. Srinivasan accompanied Dr Ambedkar to the First Round Table Conference (1930) as a representative of the Depressed Classes.

subject: history
text: Who among the following created the Soho Foundry for manufacturing steam engines?
explanation: James Watt, along with Matthew Boulton, set up the Soho Foundry (1795) in Birmingham to make steam engines.

subject: history
text: Who argued in 1853 that railways will be the forerunner of modern industry in India?
explanation: In 1853, Karl Marx wrote in the New York Daily Tribune that railways in India would bring modern industry, though under British rule.

subject: history
text: What was the name of the railway locomotive that engineer-inventor George Stephenson built in 1814?
explanation: George Stephenson built his first steam locomotive, 'Blucher', in 1814. He later built the 'Rocket' and helped start the railways in Britain.

subject: history
text: Which was the first sector of the world economy that witnessed the impact of Economic Depression?
explanation: Agriculture was the first sector to be hit by the Great Depression because farm prices fell sharply when the demand for farm products dropped.

subject: history
text: The objective of the Lex Loci Act was:
options: to regenerate Indian art and literature
to provide the right to inherit ancestral property to Hindu converts to Christianity
to create an alternate cultural-ideological system
explanation: The Lex Loci Act (Caste Disabilities Removal Act, 1850) protected the right of converts to Christianity to inherit ancestral property. It mattered to Hindus who had been disowned after conversion.

subject: history
text: To whom did Karl Marx dedicate the first volume of his seminal work 'Capital'?
explanation: Marx dedicated the first volume of 'Capital' (1867) to his friend Wilhelm Wolff, a comrade who had died in 1864, and who helped him during exile.

subject: history
text: What was the Bolshevik Party's official newspaper called?
explanation: 'Pravda' ('Truth') was the official newspaper of the Bolshevik Party. It was published from 1912 and became the newspaper of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.

subject: history
text: Which socialist thinker wrote ‘The Philosophy of Poverty’ in the 19th century?
explanation: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon wrote 'The Philosophy of Poverty' (1846). Marx wrote 'The Poverty of Philosophy' in reply.

subject: history
text: Which of the following is the parent organisation of the UN agency United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO)?
explanation: UNESCO is a specialised agency of the UN, working under the Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), which coordinates all such agencies.

subject: history
text: Which of the following is NOT an official language of the United Nations?
explanation: The six official languages of the UN are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish. Italian is not one of them.

subject: history
text: Ernst Jones of England hailed the 1857 rebellion that unmasked colonial exploitation in India. He belonged to which political group/ideology?
explanation: Ernest Jones was a Chartist leader in England who supported the 1857 rebels in India and saw it as a fight against British colonial exploitation.

subject: history
text: What was the name of Mussolini’s paramilitary group that helped him rise to power?
explanation: Mussolini's paramilitary group was the Blackshirts (squadristi), who used violence against his opponents. The Brownshirts were Hitler's group.

subject: geography
text: What is the pressure condition at the centre of an anti-cyclone?
explanation: An anticyclone is a high-pressure system. Air sinks at its centre and spreads outwards, which usually brings clear, calm weather. So the pressure at its centre is high only.

subject: geography
text: What is the name given to the imaginary line that divides the Earth into two equal halves, with one half experiencing day and the other half experiencing night?
explanation: The Circle of Illumination is the great circle that divides the Earth into a day half (lit by the Sun) and a night half. It is different from the Equator, the Prime Meridian and the International Date Line.

subject: geography
text: Which type of rock is formed by the transformation of existing rocks due to heat and pressure?
explanation: Metamorphic rocks are formed when existing rocks (igneous, sedimentary or older metamorphic rocks) are changed by heat and pressure without melting. Examples: marble from limestone and slate from shale.

subject: geography
text: The convective transfer of energy is confined only to the:
explanation: Convection (vertical movement of air) takes place mainly in the troposphere, the lowest layer, where weather occurs. The upper layers are stable, so convection is confined to the troposphere.

subject: geography
text: The temperature of the air at any place is NOT influenced by:
explanation: Air temperature depends on latitude, distance from the sea, altitude and air-mass circulation. Ocean waves do not affect the air temperature of a place.

subject: geography
text: How many major tectonic plates are there on the Earth's surface?
explanation: There are seven major tectonic plates: Pacific, North American, South American, African, Eurasian, Indo-Australian and Antarctic. Smaller plates like Nazca and Arabian are minor plates.

subject: geography
text: How many major groups of weathering processes are there?
explanation: Weathering is of three types: physical (mechanical), chemical and biological weathering. All three break down rocks in different ways.

subject: geography
text: What kind of boundary is associated with the formation of mid-ocean ridges?
explanation: Mid-ocean ridges form at divergent boundaries, where plates move apart and new crust is formed by rising magma (sea-floor spreading). The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is an example.

subject: geography
text:
Match the following types of agriculture with their characteristics and select the correct option.
Agriculture | Characteristics
A. Intensive Agriculture | 1. Slash-and-burn method
B. Extensive Agriculture | 2. High productivity per unit area
C. Shifting Agriculture | 3. Low labour and capital input
D. Plantation Agriculture | 4. Monoculture of commercial crops
explanation: Intensive farming gives high output per unit area (A-2), extensive farming uses little labour and capital on a large area (B-3), shifting agriculture uses slash-and-burn (C-1) and plantation is monoculture of commercial crops like tea and rubber (D-4).

subject: geography
text: What is an ecosystem composed of?
explanation: An ecosystem includes both living components (plants, animals, microbes) and non-living components (air, water, soil, sunlight) that interact with each other.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following rivers is a part of the Himalayan drainage system?
explanation: The Ganga is a Himalayan (perennial) river. Krishna, Godavari and Narmada belong to the Peninsular drainage system.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following rivers are part of the Himalayan drainage system?
(a) Ganga
(b) Brahmaputra
(c) Godavari
(d) Yamuna
explanation: The Ganga, Brahmaputra and Yamuna are Himalayan rivers that start in the mountains, so a, b and d are correct. The Godavari is a Peninsular river.

subject: geography
text: The company/industry in which the investment in fixed assets of plant and machinery DOES NOT exceed rupees one crore is:
explanation: As per the older classification, a small scale industry was one whose investment in plant and machinery did not exceed Rs 1 crore. Larger investment made it a medium or large industry.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following sea ports is located in Odisha and is one of the major ports on the eastern coast of India?
explanation: Paradip Port is in Odisha on India's east coast. Haldia is in West Bengal, Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and Kandla in Gujarat (west coast).

subject: geography
text: The natural vegetation of the Western Ghats is predominantly:
explanation: The Western Ghats get very heavy rainfall (over 200 cm), so they have tropical evergreen forests.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following regions of India is known for black soil, also called ‘Regur soil’, which is ideal for cotton cultivation?
explanation: Black soil (Regur) is found in the Deccan Plateau (Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP). It holds moisture well and is ideal for cotton, so it is also called 'black cotton soil'.

subject: geography
text: In disaster management, which of the following best describes the role of 'amateur radio' as an alternative communication system?
options: It ensures real-time video communication with satellite links.
It provides high-speed internet connection in remote areas.
It supports voice and text communication when other communication infrastructures fail.
It is used solely for broadcasting emergency alerts through public radio stations.
explanation: Amateur (ham) radio is useful in disasters because it can send voice and text messages when phone lines, internet and other communication fail.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is an example of an alternative communication system used during emergencies?
explanation: In an emergency when the power and networks are down, simple tools like flashlights and signal mirrors can send signals to rescuers. Phones, TV and social media all depend on networks or power.

subject: geography
text: ___________ make(s) the Northern Atlantic Ocean warmer.
options: Gulf Stream and North Equatorial current
Gulf Stream and North Atlantic drift
Gulf Stream and South Atlantic drift
explanation: The Gulf Stream and the North Atlantic Drift are warm currents that carry warm water to the northern Atlantic and warm the climate of north-western Europe.

subject: geography
text: The process of vertical heating of the atmosphere is known as:
explanation: Convection is the vertical heating of the atmosphere. Warm air rises and carries heat upwards, and cooler air comes down.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is a biological factor that contributes to soil formation?
explanation: Vegetation is a biological factor in soil formation, since plant roots and decayed leaves add humus. Wind, rainfall and temperature are climatic factors.

subject: geography
text: Gently inclined rocky floors close to the mountains at their foot, with or without a thin cover of debris, are called:
explanation: A pediment is a gently sloping rocky surface at the foot of a mountain, with or without a thin cover of debris. It is formed in dry regions by the retreat of mountain slopes.

subject: geography
text: The amount of water vapour in the atmosphere is added due to which of the following?
explanation: Water vapour enters the atmosphere mainly through evaporation from oceans, rivers and lakes. Condensation does the opposite: it removes vapour from the air.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following ocean basins is located between the Americas and Europe/Africa?
explanation: The Atlantic Ocean lies between the Americas on the west and Europe and Africa on the east.

subject: geography
text: A line graph is commonly used to show which of the following?
options: Distribution of rainfall in different regions
explanation: A line graph is best for showing changes over time, such as monthly temperature. Bar graphs are used to compare categories.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following processes are associated with the formation of block mountains?
1. Normal faulting
2. Reverse faulting
3. Tensional stress
4. Compressional stress
explanation: Block mountains are made when tensional stress pulls the crust apart and normal faulting raises a block between two faults. So only 1 and 3 are correct. Reverse faulting and compression are linked with fold mountains.

subject: geography
text: What is the angle between the Earth's axis and the plane of its orbit around the Sun?
explanation: The Earth's axis is tilted at 23.5° from the vertical, so the angle between the axis and the plane of its orbit is 66.5°.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is a tributary of the Ganga River?
explanation: The Yamuna is a major tributary of the Ganga, joining it at Prayagraj (Allahabad). Mahanadi, Godavari and Narmada are separate rivers.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is the largest biosphere reserve in India?
explanation: The Gulf of Mannar (Tamil Nadu), with about 10,500 sq km, is the largest biosphere reserve in India (area). It is known for marine life such as corals and dugongs.

subject: geography
text:
Which rivers contribute to the formation of the Sunderbans delta?
(a) Ganga
(b) Brahmaputra
(c) Yamuna
(d) Mahanadi
explanation: The Sundarbans delta, the largest delta in the world, is formed by the Ganga and Brahmaputra (with their distributaries). The Mahanadi forms its own delta in Odisha.

subject: geography
text: Which port is often referred to as the ‘Gateway of India’?
explanation: Mumbai (Bombay) is called the 'Gateway of India', as ships and travellers arrive here, and the famous monument by that name stands at its harbour.

subject: geography
text: In a food web, which organisms are responsible for breaking down dead organic matter?
explanation: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.

subject: geography
text: Which Indian state is the largest producer of sugarcane, contributing significantly to the sugar industry in India during 2023-2024?
explanation: Uttar Pradesh is India's largest sugarcane producer, followed by Maharashtra and Karnataka.

subject: geography
text:
Select the option that is true regarding the following two statements labelled Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Extensive agriculture is practiced on large land holdings with minimal labour input.
Reason (R): Extensive farming is typically found in densely populated regions of India.
options: A is false, but R is true.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
explanation: Extensive farming is done on large fields with little labour, so A is true. It is found in thinly populated areas (like the prairies), not in densely populated regions, so R is false.

subject: geography
text: In the context of disaster survival skills, what is the most effective strategy for managing stress and maintaining mental health immediately after a catastrophic event?
options: Engaging in community support activities and seeking professional counseling if needed
Focusing solely on physical recovery without addressing mental health issues
Isolating yourself from others to avoid emotional distress
Ignoring the need for professional psychological support
explanation: After a disaster, the best way to cope with stress is to stay connected with the community and take professional counselling when needed. Isolating or ignoring mental health can make things worse.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is used for detection of a Tsunami?
explanation: Tsunami detection uses satellites (and ocean buoys and pressure sensors) to watch sea level changes. Seismographs detect earthquakes, but they cannot detect the wave itself.

subject: geography
text: What is the primary characteristic that distinguishes intrusive igneous rocks from extrusive igneous rocks?
options: Intrusive rocks form from volcanic eruptions.
Intrusive rocks have larger crystals due to slow cooling.
Extrusive rocks are harder than intrusive rocks.
Extrusive rocks contain more metallic minerals.
explanation: Intrusive igneous rocks cool slowly deep in the Earth, so they have large crystals (like granite). Extrusive rocks cool fast on the surface and have small crystals (like basalt).

subject: geography
text: Which of the following factors is the primary cause of ocean waves?
options: Wind blowing over the surface of the ocean
explanation: Ocean waves are mainly caused by wind blowing over the surface of the water. Tides are caused by the moon's pull, and currents by winds, temperature and salinity.

subject: geography
text: The air temperature at the tropopause is about:
options: −35°C over the equator and about −80°C over the poles
−80°C over the equator and about −45°C over the poles
−80°C over the equator and about −35°C over the poles
−45°C over the equator and about −80°C over the poles
explanation: The tropopause is coldest above the equator, at about -80 degrees C, and warmer over the poles at about -45 degrees C, because the troposphere is thicker at the equator.

subject: geography
text: The high-pressure areas known as the subtropical highs is found along:
explanation: The subtropical high-pressure belts lie at about 30° N and 30° S, where the air that rises at the equator sinks.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following processes are involved in the movement of tectonic plates?
1. Mantle convection
2. Ridge push
3. Slab pull
4. Gravitational collapse
explanation: Plates move because of mantle convection currents, ridge push and slab pull. Gravitational collapse is not a driver of plate movement.

subject: geography
text: Normally, temperature decreases with altitude, but when it increases with height, the phenomenon is called:
explanation: Normally temperature falls with height. When it rises with height instead, the situation is called temperature inversion.

subject: geography
text: When two tectonic plates move away from each other, what type of boundary is formed?
explanation: When two plates move away from each other, the boundary is divergent (constructive). New crust forms in the gap.

subject: geography
text: In Koppen’s climate classification, the characteristic - the average temperature of the coldest month of the (mid-latitude) climate years being higher than −3°C but below 18°C - refers to which climate group?
explanation: In the Koppen scheme the C group (warm temperate, mid-latitude) has the coldest month between -3 degrees C and 18 degrees C. The A group (tropical) is above 18 degrees C and the D group is below -3 degrees C.

subject: geography
text: The chief chemical in limestone is:
explanation: Limestone is mainly calcium carbonate (CaCO3). It is a sedimentary rock and it fizzes when dilute acid is added.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is/are NOT a reason for tsunamis?
explanation: Tsunamis are caused by undersea earthquakes, volcanic eruptions and underwater landslides. The moon's pull causes tides, not tsunamis.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following sectors contribute significantly to India's fisheries industry?
a) Inland fisheries
b) Marine fisheries
c) Mining activities
d) Agricultural farming
explanation: India's fishing industry includes inland fisheries (rivers, lakes, ponds) and marine fisheries (sea). Mining and farming are different sectors.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is an example of a freshwater ecosystem?
explanation: A lake is a freshwater ecosystem. Oceans are saltwater (marine) ecosystems, and forests and deserts are terrestrial ecosystems.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following describes the drainage patterns resembling the branches of a tree?
explanation: A dendritic drainage pattern looks like the branches of a tree, and forms where the rock is of uniform type. Trellis looks like a garden fence, radial spreads out from a hill and rectangular follows joints.

subject: geography
text: The major factors influencing the distribution of manufacturing industries include __________, __________, and __________.
explanation: The location of industries is mainly decided by the availability of raw materials, labour and transport (as well as power and markets).

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is NOT a crop associated with dry agriculture in India?
explanation: Dry farming is done in areas with less rainfall and grows drought-resistant crops like millets, pulses and groundnut. Sugarcane needs a lot of water, so it is not a dry-farming crop.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following rivers fall into the Bay of Bengal?
(a) Godavari
(b) Krishna
(c) Narmada
(d) Kaveri
explanation: The Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri flow east into the Bay of Bengal. The Narmada flows west into the Arabian Sea.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is the primary reason for the intensification of the south-west monsoon in India?
options: High pressure over the Indian Ocean
Intense low pressure over the Tibetan Plateau
Cold winds coming from the Himalayas
explanation: In summer the Tibetan Plateau gets very hot, and intense low pressure develops over it. This pulls in the moist south-west monsoon winds and intensifies the monsoon.

subject: geography
text: As tsunami waves approach the shoreline, ____________.
options: both the speed and the height of the waves increase
only the height of the waves increases
only the speed of the waves increases
there is no effect on the waves
explanation: As a tsunami reaches the shallow coast, its speed drops but its height rises sharply. This is why it becomes very destructive near the shore.

subject: geography
text: Long-wave radiation is absorbed by atmospheric gases, especially __________.
explanation: The Earth gives out long-wave radiation, which is absorbed mainly by carbon dioxide and water vapour, the main greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

subject: geography
text: Exfoliation can be caused by expansion and contraction induced by changes in __________.
explanation: Exfoliation happens when rocks expand in the heat of day and contract at night, so the outer layers peel off in sheets. It is caused by changes in temperature.

subject: geography
text: The Sahel region is located in the ______ of the Sahara Desert.
explanation: The Sahel is a semi-arid belt lying to the south of the Sahara Desert in Africa, stretching from Senegal to Sudan.

subject: geography
text: What is the main cause of evaporation?
explanation: Temperature is the main cause of evaporation. A higher temperature gives water molecules more energy, so more water turns to vapour.

subject: geography
text: How much time does the Earth take to complete one rotation on its axis?
explanation: The Earth takes 23 hours 56 minutes 4 seconds (a sidereal day) to rotate once on its axis. A day is counted as 24 hours because of the Earth's motion around the Sun.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following processes is important in heating the lower layers of the atmosphere?
explanation: The ground is heated by the sun and passes its heat to the air touching it by conduction, which heats the lowest layers of the atmosphere. Conduction is important only near the surface.

subject: geography
text: Which rivers in India are called 'perennial' rivers?
explanation: Perennial rivers have water throughout the year. The Indus, Ganga and Yamuna are fed by glaciers and rain, and the Kaveri gets rain in both monsoons, so they flow round the year. Narmada and Tapi mostly depend on the monsoon.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following states are major producers of mica in India?
a) Rajasthan
b) Gujarat
c) Andhra Pradesh
d) Karnataka
explanation: Mica in India is mainly produced in Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh (along with Jharkhand and Bihar). Gujarat and Karnataka are not major mica producers.

subject: geography
text: In disaster management, which is the important component of 'contingency planning' that enhances preparedness and response efficiency?
options: Designing context-specific response strategies supported by regular training exercises and simulations
Prioritising only long-term development projects and neglecting immediate response mechanisms
Relying entirely on international relief assistance without establishing local response capacity
Focusing only on post-disaster rehabilitation measures without pre-disaster preparedness planning
explanation: Contingency planning means planning ahead for possible disasters. It works best with local response plans and regular training, drills and simulations. Ignoring preparedness or depending only on outside help does not work.

subject: geography
text: In which of the following regions are temperate forests in India mainly found?
explanation: Temperate (montane) forests of India are found in the Himalayas above about 2000 m, where it is cool, with trees like oak, chestnut and spruce.

subject: geography
text: Which is the busiest airport in India in terms of cargo handling?
options: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata
explanation: The Indira Gandhi International Airport in Delhi handles the most cargo among Indian airports (with Mumbai close behind).

subject: geography
text: Which of the following crops is mainly associated with wet farming in India?
explanation: Wet farming is done in regions with plenty of rainfall or irrigation, and rice is the main wet-farming crop. Wheat, millet and cotton are grown with less water.

subject: geography
text: Evaporation is a process by which water changes from _________.
explanation: Evaporation is the change of water from a liquid to a gas (water vapour), which happens when water is heated by the sun.

subject: geography
text: What are the local winds called during the summer season in northern India?
explanation: In northern India, hot dry local winds called 'Loo' blow in summer afternoons. Haboob is a Sudan wind and Chinook is a warm wind of the Rockies.

subject: geography
text: According to the continental drift theory, which supercontinent existed around 300 million years ago?
explanation: About 300 million years ago, all continents were joined in a single supercontinent called Pangaea, proposed by Alfred Wegener in his continental drift theory. Gondwana and Laurasia were its southern and northern parts.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following causes the change of seasons on the Earth?
options: The combination of the tilt of the Earth's axis and its orbit around the Sun
Rotation of the Earth on its axis
Distance of the Earth from the Sun
Movement of the Moon around the Earth
explanation: Seasons change because the Earth's axis is tilted and it revolves around the Sun, so different parts get sunlight at different angles during the year. Rotation causes day and night.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following options is NOT an example of a metamorphic rock?
explanation: Slate, marble and gneiss are metamorphic rocks. Basalt is an extrusive igneous rock formed from cooled lava.

subject: geography
text: Heave, Flow and Slide represent which of the following processes?
explanation: Heave, flow and slide are types of mass movement, in which rocks and soil move down a slope under gravity, without the help of water or wind as a carrying agent.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is an example of convection?
options: Heat is transferred from the hands to a piece of ice, as a result of which the ice melts when held in the hands.
Warm water around the equator moves towards the poles, while cold water at the poles moves towards the equator.
Cold air around the equator moves towards the poles, while warm air at the poles moves towards the equator.
Alpha particles are emitted during the decaying of Uranium-238 into Thorium-234.
explanation: Convection is the transfer of heat through the movement of a fluid (liquid or gas). Ocean water warmed at the equator moving to the poles, and cold water coming back, is an example. Heat passing from hands to ice is conduction.

subject: geography
text: 88 percent of the total water entering the atmosphere comes from the ocean between _____________.
explanation: About 88% of the water vapour entering the atmosphere comes from the oceans between 60 degrees N and 60 degrees S latitudes, where temperatures are high.

subject: geography
text:
Match the following rivers with their places of origin.
Rivers | Origin
(A) Ganga | (1) Amarkantak Plateau
(B) Narmada | (2) Mansarovar Lake
(C) Brahmaputra | (3) Gangotri Glacier
(D) Godavari | (4) Nashik, Maharashtra
explanation: The Ganga starts from the Gangotri Glacier, the Narmada from Amarkantak, the Brahmaputra from Mansarovar Lake area and the Godavari from Nashik (Trimbakeshwar), so A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4.

subject: geography
text: In the context of alternative communication, what help does 'signalling with flags' provide?
options: Provides immediate visual signals for communication over short distances.
explanation: Signalling with flags gives quick visual signals over short distances when phones and internet are not working. It does not send digital messages or improve the internet.

subject: geography
text: Mohan is a small-scale industry worker. What is the most uncommon feature of this institution?
options: It contributes to the local economy.
It has vast access to skilled labour and technology.
explanation: Small-scale industries usually have limited access to skilled labour and technology, which is why this is their least common feature. They promote rural development, help local economies and decentralise production.

subject: geography
text: Shifting cultivation, also known as _____, is widely practised in the north-eastern states of India, where forests are cleared and burnt for agricultural purposes.
explanation: Shifting cultivation is called 'Jhum' in the north-eastern states of India. Farmers clear and burn a patch of forest, grow crops for a few years and then move to a new patch.

subject: geography
text: The Ganga-Brahmaputra delta is also known as the ________.
explanation: The Ganga-Brahmaputra delta is also called the Sundarban Delta, after the sundari trees found in its mangrove forests. It is the largest delta in the world.

subject: geography
text: In the context of disaster management, how does the 'shared responsibility model' contribute to effective crisis response and recovery?
options: Collaboration among the government, communities and individuals
Transferring all duties to external agencies
explanation: In the shared responsibility model the government, communities and individuals all work together in disaster management. No single agency can handle a large disaster alone.

subject: geography
text: What is the primary source of energy for most ecosystems?
explanation: Sunlight is the main source of energy for almost every ecosystem, because green plants use it to make food (photosynthesis), which then passes to other organisms.

subject: geography
text: Which state experiences the North-westerlies (Nor'westers) or Kalbaisakhi in the summer season?
explanation: Kalbaisakhi (Nor'westers) are thunderstorms in the pre-monsoon (summer) season in West Bengal and nearby areas. They bring short heavy showers and are good for tea, jute and rice.

subject: geography
text: What are the primary components of granite?
explanation: Granite, an intrusive igneous rock, is mainly made of feldspar, quartz and mica.

subject: geography
text: The wind direction pattern in an anticyclone in the Northern Hemisphere is ________.
explanation: In the Northern Hemisphere the winds in an anticyclone (high pressure) spiral clockwise because of the Coriolis effect. In a cyclone they blow anticlockwise.

subject: geography
text: The Tropic of Cancer passes through which of the following countries?
explanation: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5 degrees N) passes through India, in states like Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Australia, Argentina and Brazil lie on the Tropic of Capricorn.

subject: geography
text: What is the main disadvantage of using hachures to show relief on a map?
options: It is suitable only for flat terrain
It requires the use of colours
It is difficult to use for large areas
It does not provide quantitative elevation information
explanation: Hachures are small lines drawn to show slopes, but they do not give the exact height (elevation) of a place. Contours do that.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following continents was a part of the ancient supercontinent Gondwana?
explanation: Gondwana was the southern supercontinent made of South America, Africa, Antarctica, Australia and India. Europe, Asia and North America were part of Laurasia.

subject: geography
text: The physical process of weathering is also called ___________.
explanation: Physical weathering breaks rocks without changing their chemistry, using forces like temperature change and frost, so it is also called mechanical weathering.

subject: geography
text: After being heated, the Earth becomes a radiating body and it radiates energy into the atmosphere ____________.
options: mainly as short-waves and partially as long-waves
explanation: The Sun sends short-wave radiation, but the heated Earth re-radiates energy only as long-wave (infrared) radiation. This is terrestrial radiation.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following years relate to the declaration of the Kyoto Protocol and its coming into force, respectively?
explanation: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in 1997 and came into force in 2005. It was an agreement to limit greenhouse gas emissions.

subject: geography
text: In the context of disaster management, how does the 'shared responsibility model' contribute to effective crisis response and recovery?
options: By ensuring that multiple stakeholders, including the government, community organisations and individuals, cooperate and share roles to enhance overall disaster management efficiency
By focusing only on the economic recovery of the affected areas while neglecting social and environmental aspects
By centralising all decision-making processes in a single agency
By handing over complete responsibility to external agencies without involving local stakeholders
explanation: In the shared responsibility model, the government, community organisations and individuals cooperate and share tasks for better disaster management. It does not focus only on economic recovery or one agency.

subject: geography
text: Through which of the following states does the Mahanadi river flow before joining the Bay of Bengal?
explanation: The Mahanadi rises in Chhattisgarh, flows through Odisha and falls into the Bay of Bengal.

subject: geography
text: What is the main reason for rainfall in winter in North India?
explanation: Winter rainfall in north India is caused by Western Disturbances, which are weather systems coming from the Mediterranean. This rain is good for the rabi crop, especially wheat.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following factors affect the location of manufacturing industries?
A) Labour availability
B) Government policies
C) Climatic conditions
D) Land cost
explanation: The location of industries is affected by labour availability, government policy, climate and land cost. All four are correct.

subject: geography
text: _______ is the longest highway tunnel in the world.
explanation: The Atal Tunnel in Himachal Pradesh (Rohtang, opened 2020) is about 9.02 km long and is the longest highway tunnel in the world above 10,000 feet.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following options is NOT an important resource for establishing an industry?
explanation: Raw materials, human resources (workers) and capital are essential for setting up an industry. Fertile land is important for farming, but not necessary for industry.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is a characteristic of dry farming in India?
options: Use of irrigation canals for water supply
Cultivation of crops with high water requirements
Growing crops in areas of low rainfall
explanation: Dry farming is done in areas with low rainfall, using drought-resistant crops like millets, pulses and groundnut. Rice and jute need a lot of water.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following options best defines a food web?
options: Flow of energy in an ecosystem
A sequence of plants and animals in an ecosystem
explanation: A food web is a group of many food chains that are connected with each other in an ecosystem. A single food chain is only a straight line of who eats whom.

subject: geography
text:
The northern plains of India are an important part of the country's geography for several reasons. Which of the following statements is true regarding the northern plains?
i) They are formed by the alluvial deposits of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers.
ii) These plains are fertile and densely populated.
iii) The plains are prone to frequent floods due to river overflow.
iv) Black soil is abundant in the northern plains.
explanation: The northern plains are made of alluvium brought by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra. They are fertile, densely populated and prone to floods. Black soil is found in the Deccan, so statement iv is wrong.

subject: geography
text: Sand dunes are formed in which of the following?
explanation: Sand dunes are formed in deserts, where the wind blows and deposits sand into mounds and ridges.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following are the characteristics of the Earth's crust?
I. It is the outermost layer of the Earth.
II. It is mainly composed of silicate rocks.
III. Continental crust is thicker than oceanic crust.
IV. It is mainly in a liquid state.
explanation: The crust is the outermost, solid layer, mainly of silicate rocks, and the continental crust is thicker than the oceanic crust. The crust is not liquid, so IV is wrong.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following does NOT occur during an equinox?
options: Occurrence of the spring and autumn equinoxes.
The Earth is at its closest point to the Sun.
The Sun is directly above the equator.
The duration of day and night is equal globally.
explanation: On an equinox the Sun is above the equator and day and night are equal. The Earth is closest to the Sun (perihelion) in early January, so this is not an equinox event.

subject: geography
text: The circulation of air in an anticyclone is ___________.
explanation: In an anticyclone, air sinks (goes down) at the centre and spreads outward at the surface, so the circulation is downward and outward.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following factors is the main cause of ocean waves?
options: Winds blowing over the sea surface
Difference in temperature in sea water
explanation: Ocean waves are mainly caused by winds blowing across the sea surface. Tides are caused by the moon and sun.

subject: geography
text: According to which law does the total radiated energy of an object increase with rising temperature, and the peak of the emitted spectrum shift towards shorter wavelengths?
explanation: Wien's Law says that as an object gets hotter, the peak of the radiation it gives off moves to shorter wavelengths. The total energy given off also increases with temperature (Stefan-Boltzmann Law).

subject: geography
text: A greenhouse is made up of glass which is ________.
options: opaque to incoming long-wave solar radiation and transparent to outgoing short-wave radiation
transparent to incoming short-wave solar radiation and opaque to outgoing long-wave radiation
opaque to incoming short-wave solar radiation and transparent to outgoing long-wave radiation
transparent to incoming long-wave solar radiation and opaque to outgoing short-wave radiation
explanation: Glass lets in short-wave sunlight but traps the long-wave heat rays coming out. This is why a greenhouse stays warm, and it is similar to the greenhouse effect of the atmosphere.

subject: geography
text: What type of rock is formed by the cooling of molten magma below the Earth's surface?
explanation: Intrusive igneous rocks are formed when magma cools slowly below the Earth's surface, for example granite. Extrusive rocks form when lava cools on the surface.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following types of industry produces raw material for other industries?
explanation: The iron and steel industry is a basic (key) industry because its output is the raw material for many other industries such as machinery and automobiles.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following industrial clusters are mainly associated with textile production in India?
A) Surat
B) Tiruppur
C) Kanpur
D) Jodhpur
explanation: Surat, Tiruppur, Kanpur and Jodhpur are all textile clusters. Surat is known for synthetic fabric, Tiruppur for knitwear, Kanpur for cotton/wool and Jodhpur for textiles and handicrafts.

subject: geography
text: In which of the following regions of India is wet farming practised?
explanation: Wet farming is done in regions of high rainfall or with irrigation, such as Eastern India (West Bengal, Assam, Odisha). Western Rajasthan is dry.

subject: geography
text: The Godavari river is often called the ______.
explanation: The Godavari, the longest peninsular river, is called the 'Dakshin Ganga' (South Ganga), because of its size and sacredness.

subject: geography
text:
Identify the factors responsible for the uneven distribution of rainfall in India.
a) Latitude of the region
b) Topography and physical features
c) Distance from the sea
d) Global wind patterns only
explanation: Rainfall in India is unevenly distributed because of latitude, mountains and other physical features and distance from the sea. Global winds alone do not explain it.

subject: geography
text: What was the cause of the tsunami in Japan in 2011?
options: Landslide in the sea due to seismic activity
Earthquake in the sea near the Tohoku region
explanation: The 2011 tsunami in Japan was caused by a powerful undersea earthquake (magnitude 9) near Tohoku, in the Pacific Ocean.

subject: geography
text:
Match the following rivers with their lengths.
Rivers | Length
(A) Kaveri Basin | (1) 760 km
(B) Mahanadi Basin | (2) 860 km
(C) Krishna Basin | (3) 1400 km
(D) Godavari Basin | (4) 1500 km
explanation: The lengths are Kaveri 760 km, Mahanadi 860 km, Krishna 1400 km and Godavari 1500 km, so the matching is A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.

subject: geography
text: To share the responsibility of dealing with disasters, the World Conference on Natural Disaster Reduction was held in Yokohama city in __________.
explanation: The World Conference on Natural Disaster Reduction was held in Yokohama, Japan in 1994. It adopted the Yokohama Strategy for a safer world.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is a consequence of Earth’s rotation?
options: Variation in solar radiation at different latitudes
explanation: Earth's rotation causes the Coriolis effect, which deflects winds and ocean currents (to the right in the Northern Hemisphere). Seasons come from the Earth's revolution and tilt.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following phenomena can occur as a result of the interaction between tectonic plates?
1. Earthquakes
2. Tsunamis
3. Mountain formation
4. Subduction of oceanic plates
explanation: When plates interact they cause earthquakes, tsunamis (undersea), mountain formation and the subduction of oceanic plates. All four are correct.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is NOT a type of 'Major rock'?
explanation: The three major rock types are igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic. 'Blended rocks' is not a type.

subject: geography
text: How many major groups of weathering process are there?
explanation: There are three groups of weathering: physical, chemical and biological.

subject: geography
text: Europe witnessed ‘Little Ice Age’ from:
explanation: The 'Little Ice Age' in Europe was a cold period lasting from about 1300 to 1850, with cold winters and glaciers advancing.

subject: geography
text: The transformation of water vapour into water is called:
explanation: Condensation is the change of water vapour into liquid water (drops), which forms clouds, dew and fog.

subject: geography
text: What are isohyets on a map?
options: Lines connecting places with equal wind speed
Lines connecting places with equal pressure
Lines connecting places with equal rainfall
Lines connecting places with equal temperature
explanation: Isohyets are lines on a map joining places that receive equal rainfall. Isotherms join equal temperature, isobars equal pressure.

subject: geography
text: Which seismic waves are responsible for traveling through both solids and liquids?
explanation: P-waves (primary waves) are longitudinal and can travel through solids, liquids and gases. S-waves (secondary waves) travel only through solids, which is how we know the Earth's outer core is liquid.

subject: geography
text: In a marine ecosystem, which of the following is likely to be a primary producer?
explanation: Phytoplankton, the tiny floating plants of the sea, make food by photosynthesis, so they are the primary producers of marine ecosystems. Sharks, jellyfish and zooplankton are consumers.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is an example of a modern small industry?
explanation: Powerloom is a modern small industry that uses machines. Khadi, handicrafts and coir are traditional industries that depend on hand work.

subject: geography
text: In the mitigation of landslide hazards, what is the function of 'geotextiles'?
options: To improve the aesthetic appearance of construction sites
To reinforce soil and stabilise slopes by providing support and preventing erosion
To increase the drainage capacity of land
To detect early signs of landslides through monitoring
explanation: Geotextiles are strong fabrics placed in the ground to strengthen the soil and stabilise slopes, and they help prevent erosion and slides.

subject: geography
text:
The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats differ significantly in terms of their physical features. Which of the following statements are correct about these two ranges?
i) The Western Ghats are continuous and have a greater height compared to the Eastern Ghats.
ii) The Eastern Ghats are more eroded and discontinuous.
iii) The Western Ghats receive heavy rainfall, while the Eastern Ghats are relatively drier.
iv) Both ranges are known for the presence of several active volcanoes.
explanation: The Western Ghats are higher, continuous and get heavy rain. The Eastern Ghats are lower, broken by rivers and drier. Neither has active volcanoes, so statement iv is wrong.

subject: geography
text:
Match the following industries with their respective key locations.
Industry | Key Location
A. Cotton Textile | 1. Jamshedpur
B. Iron and Steel | 2. Ahmedabad
C. Cotton Processing | 3. Coimbatore
D. Steel Production | 4. Bhilai
explanation: Cotton textile: Ahmedabad. Iron and steel: Jamshedpur. Cotton processing: Coimbatore. Steel production: Bhilai. So A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4.

subject: geography
text:
Which three of the following animals are found in India's desert ecosystems?
a) Blackbuck
b) Asiatic Lion
c) Chinkara
d) Indian Wild Ass
explanation: Blackbuck, chinkara and the Indian wild ass are found in desert and semi-desert areas of India such as Rajasthan and the Rann of Kachchh. The Asiatic lion lives in the Gir forest.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is the longest National Highway in India?
explanation: NH-44 (Srinagar to Kanyakumari, about 3,700 km) is the longest national highway in India.

subject: geography
text: What is the main objective of having a 'disaster preparedness plan'?
options: To delay the response until all resources are available
To ensure that there is no need for evacuation
To only focus on repairing damaged infrastructure after a disaster
To outline steps to take before, during and after a disaster to ensure safety and effective response
explanation: A disaster preparedness plan lists what to do before, during and after a disaster so that people stay safe and the response is fast and organised.

subject: geography
text: The Lakshadweep Islands are located in which water body?
explanation: The Lakshadweep Islands are in the Arabian Sea, off the coast of Kerala, on the western side of India. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are in the Bay of Bengal.

subject: geography
text: Overland flow and linear flow are the two components of:
explanation: Running water has two components: overland flow (sheet flow over the surface) and linear flow (streams and rivers in valleys). Both erode and shape the land.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following phenomena is directly associated with the Earth's axial tilt?
explanation: The tilt of the Earth's axis (23.5 degrees) causes the seasons and changes in temperature. Eclipses and tides are caused by the position of the Moon.

subject: geography
text: Which rays are required to pass through a greater depth of the atmosphere?
explanation: Slanting rays travel a longer path through the atmosphere than vertical rays, so more of their energy is absorbed, reflected or scattered.

subject: geography
text: Which metamorphic rock is known for use in roofing and flooring material due to its ability to split into thin sheets?
explanation: Slate is a metamorphic rock formed from shale. It splits easily into thin flat sheets, so it is used for roofing and flooring.

subject: geography
text: Layer tinting, used in physical maps, is a method that involves:
options: using lines to represent steep and gentle slopes
using different colours to represent different elevations
using shading to represent elevation changes
drawing dashed lines to represent contours
explanation: Layer tinting (hypsometric tints) uses different colours for different heights: for example green for plains, brown for hills, white for high snowy peaks.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following processes is most likely to create mountain ranges?
explanation: Folding of the Earth's crust, caused by compressive forces where plates collide, forms mountain ranges such as the Himalayas and the Alps.

subject: geography
text: The depth of the continental slope region varies between:
explanation: The continental slope is the steep slope that lies between the continental shelf and the deep ocean floor, with depths of roughly 200 m to 3000 m.

subject: geography
text: After the condensation of water vapour, the release of moisture is known as:
explanation: After water vapour condenses, the release of moisture as rain, snow or hail is called precipitation.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following rivers flows through a rift valley?
explanation: The Narmada flows westward in a rift valley (a long trough formed by faulting) between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges, so it has no delta but forms an estuary.

subject: geography
text:
Read the given assertion (A) and reason (R) and select the most appropriate option.
(A): The sugar industry in India has a significant impact on rural employment. (R): Sugarcane cultivation requires a large workforce for planting, harvesting, and processing.
options: A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
explanation: The sugar industry gives jobs to lakhs of rural people. The cane needs many workers for planting, harvesting and processing, so R explains A.

subject: geography
text: Why is it important to use safety helmets at a construction site?
options: To protect workers from head injuries caused by falling objects
To keep the workers warm in cold weather
explanation: Helmets protect workers from head injuries caused by falling objects at construction sites, which is a basic safety rule.

subject: geography
text: The phenomenon of 'October Heat' in India is experienced due to which of the following?
options: cold winds blowing from the Himalayas
cyclonic disturbances in the Bay of Bengal
high temperature and humidity after the retreat of the monsoon
explanation: 'October heat' is the hot and humid weather in October, after the south-west monsoon retreats. The ground is still moist and the sun is strong, so it feels sticky.

subject: geography
text: The Konkan Railway runs through which geographical region?
explanation: The Konkan Railway (Mumbai to Mangaluru) passes along the western coast and crosses the Western Ghats, using many tunnels and bridges.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following statements describes the Shiwalik Range in the Himalayan system?
i) It is the outermost range of the Himalayas.
ii) The valleys located between the Shiwaliks and the Lesser Himalayas are called Duns.
iii) It is composed of unconsolidated sediments brought down by rivers from the higher ranges.
iv) It is the highest range in the Himalayan system.
explanation: The Shiwaliks are the outermost and lowest ranges of the Himalayas, made of loose sediments brought by rivers. The valleys between them and the Lesser Himalayas are called Duns. The Himadri is the highest range, so statement iv is wrong.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following regions is known for dry agriculture in India?
explanation: Western Rajasthan is dry and gets little rain, so dry farming with millets and pulses is done here. Delta and plains regions have more water.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is a key factor in attracting investment to the industrial sector?
explanation: Skilled labour is one of the main factors that attract industries to an area. High land revenue, strict rules and poor transport put investors off.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following three states are major producers of bananas in India?
a) Andhra Pradesh
b) Maharashtra
c) Gujarat
d) Karnataka
explanation: Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka (with Tamil Nadu and Gujarat also growing) are among the major banana producers of India.

subject: geography
text: The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats meet at which of the following hills?
explanation: The Western and Eastern Ghats meet at the Nilgiri Hills in the south of the Deccan Plateau.

subject: geography
text: The places near the sea-level record _______ as compared to the places situated at higher elevations.
explanation: Air is thicker and holds more heat near sea level, and temperature falls with height (about 6.5 degrees C per km). So places near sea level are warmer than places at higher elevations.

subject: geography
text: The formation of humus in soil is primarily due to the decay of:
explanation: Humus is the dark, rich part of the soil formed by the decay of dead plants and animals (organic matter). It makes the soil fertile.

subject: geography
text: What is the name given to the imaginary line that divides the Earth into two equal halves, one half experiencing day and the other half experiencing night?
explanation: The terminator (circle of illumination) is the line that separates the day side and the night side of the Earth.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is NOT considered evidence for continental drift?
explanation: Evidence for continental drift includes the fit of continents, matching rocks and mountain ranges, and similar fossils across oceans. The depth of oceans is not evidence.

subject: geography
text: The primary Greenhouse Gases (GHGs) of concern today are:
options: Carbon Dioxide, Nitrous Oxide, Carbon Monoxide, Ozone
Carbon Dioxide, Nitrous Oxide, Methane, Ozone
Carbon Dioxide, Nitric Oxide, Methane, Ozone
Carbon Dioxide, Nitrous Oxide, Methane, Sulphur
explanation: The main greenhouse gases are carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and ozone (also CFCs). Carbon monoxide is not a greenhouse gas of primary concern.

subject: geography
text: The effects of earthquakes can vary based on certain conditions. Which of the following statements about earthquake effects are accurate? I. Shallow-focus earthquakes typically cause more damage than deep-focus earthquakes. II. Earthquake damage is generally more severe in areas with loose, unconsolidated soils. III. Earthquakes cannot trigger landslides or tsunamis. IV. The Richter scale measures the magnitude of an earthquake, not its intensity.
explanation: Shallow-focus earthquakes are more damaging, loose soil makes damage worse, and the Richter scale measures magnitude. Earthquakes can also trigger landslides and tsunamis, so III is wrong.

subject: geography
text: What is the pressure condition at the centre of an anti-cyclone?
explanation: The centre of an anticyclone has high pressure, with sinking air spreading outwards, which usually gives clear weather.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following graphs is best suited for comparing annual rainfall across multiple regions?
explanation: A bar plot is the best way to compare values (like annual rainfall) across several regions. Line graphs show changes over time.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following states is the largest producer of maize in India?
explanation: Karnataka is the largest producer of maize in India, followed by Madhya Pradesh.

subject: geography
text: The 'stage 3' of the demographic transition model is characterised by:
options: high birth rates and declining death rates
high birth rates and high death rates
low birth rates and low death rates
rapid population growth due to declining birth rates and low death rates
explanation: In stage 3 of the demographic transition, birth rates decline, and death rates are low, which gives fast population growth that gradually slows down.

subject: geography
text:
Arrange the following stages of shifting cultivation in the correct order.
1. Felling of forests
2. Harvesting of crops
3. Burning of vegetation
4. Cultivating the land
5. Abandonment of the land
explanation: The correct order of shifting cultivation is: felling of forests, burning of vegetation, cultivating the land, harvesting and abandonment of the land. Abandonment allows the soil to recover.

subject: geography
text: Through which state does the south-west monsoon enter India?
explanation: The south-west monsoon first arrives in India on the Kerala coast, around 1 June.

subject: geography
text: The Deccan Plateau is an example of which type of landform?
explanation: The Deccan Plateau is made of lava from ancient volcanic eruptions (Deccan Traps) so it is a volcanic plateau in the peninsular block.

subject: geography
text:
The Northern Plains of India are a vital part of the country’s geography for several reasons. Which of the following statements is correct about the Northern Plains?
i) They are formed by the alluvial deposits of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers.
ii) These plains are fertile and are densely populated.
iii) The plains are prone to frequent flooding due to river overflow.
iv) The soils in the Northern Plains are rich in black soil.
explanation: The northern plains are made of alluvium from the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra. They are fertile, densely populated and flood-prone. Black soil is in the Deccan, so statement iv is wrong.

subject: geography
text: The speed of Earth’s rotation is fastest at:
explanation: The Earth's rotation speed is highest at the equator (about 1670 km/h) because the equator is the widest circle. It decreases towards the poles.

subject: geography
text: The Sahel region is situated:
explanation: The Sahel is a semi-arid strip just south of the Sahara Desert, stretching across Africa from Senegal to Sudan.

subject: geography
text: Which type of erosion is primarily caused by overland flow?
explanation: Sheet erosion is caused by overland flow. Water moves as a thin sheet over the land and removes the top layer of soil evenly.

subject: geography
text: What is a critical component of 'contingency planning' in disaster management that enhances preparedness and response efficiency?
options: Developing long-term economic recovery plans without immediate response strategies
Relying solely on external aid for disaster response without local preparations
Creating detailed, scenario-specific response plans and conducting regular drills and simulations
Focusing exclusively on post-disaster recovery without considering pre-disaster measures
explanation: Contingency planning means making detailed plans for likely scenarios and practising them through regular drills and simulations, so the response is quick.

subject: geography
text: Which region in India is most commonly associated with out-migration due to drought and water scarcity?
explanation: Rajasthan is prone to droughts and water scarcity, so many people migrate out of the state for work, especially from the western desert areas.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is the highest peak in the Himalayas located in India?
explanation: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m, Sikkim) is the highest peak of the Himalayas within India. Everest is in Nepal, K2 is in Pakistan-administered area and Nanda Devi is lower.

subject: geography
text:
Which of the following minerals are India’s major exports in the global market?
a) Iron ore
b) Bauxite
c) Gold
d) Mica
explanation: Iron ore and mica are among India's important mineral exports. Bauxite and gold exports are smaller, since India imports large amounts of gold.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following is a manmade disaster?
explanation: Volcanic eruptions, earthquakes and tsunamis are natural disasters. A road accident is caused by human action or negligence, so it is a man-made disaster.

subject: geography
text: Which of the following best explains the seasonal reversal of winds in the Indian subcontinent during monsoon?
options: High pressure over the Bay of Bengal
Differential heating and cooling of land and water
explanation: The monsoon winds reverse their direction between summer and winter due to differential heating and cooling of land and sea. This makes a low pressure over land in summer and high pressure in winter.

subject: economics
text:
Which of the following statements regarding support price is/are correct?
1. It is the price at which the government purchases crops from farmers.
2. It is designed to incentivise farmers to grow particular crops.
3. It ensures that farmers get a minimum guaranteed price even when market prices fall.
4. It applies to all food grains including fruits and vegetables.
explanation: Minimum Support Price (MSP) is the price at which the government buys crops from farmers. It guarantees a minimum price even if the market price falls, and it encourages farmers to grow particular crops. It is announced only for certain crops, not for fruits and vegetables, so statement 4 is wrong.

subject: economics
text: Which of the following is a key factor in converting a population into a productive resource?
options: Expanding the geographical area of a country
Providing access to basic education and vocational training
explanation: Population becomes a productive resource (human capital) when people get education, health care and vocational training that improve their skills. More industries or land alone do not do that.

subject: economics
text: Which of the following does NOT explain the term economic development?
options: Decrease in the rank in HDI
explanation: Economic development means better technology, better distribution, higher per capita income and a better quality of life. A fall in the HDI (Human Development Index) rank shows less development, so it does not explain the term.

subject: economics
text: Which committee's recommendations led to the revision of the poverty line calculation in India in 2009?
explanation: The Tendulkar Committee (2009) revised the method of measuring the poverty line, moving from calorie intake to monthly per capita expenditure. Later the Rangarajan Committee (2014) reviewed it again.

subject: economics
text: ____________ issues currency in India.
explanation: In India, the currency notes (except the one-rupee note and coins) are issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank. The Government of India issues coins and one-rupee notes.

subject: economics
text: Which organisation provides guidelines for sustainable development globally?
explanation: The United Nations gives the global framework for sustainable development, for example through the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

subject: economics
text: The Sen Index is associated with the measurement of which of the following social problems?
explanation: The Sen Index, given by economist Amartya Sen, measures poverty. It looks at the number of poor, how poor they are and how income is distributed among them.

subject: economics
text: Commercial banks offered loans so that money supply in the economy ____________________.
explanation: When commercial banks give loans, the borrower's money is deposited and used again in the economy, so the money supply increases (credit creation).

subject: economics
text: What was one of the vital features of the Green Revolution in India?
options: Decreased use of fertilisers and pesticides
explanation: The Green Revolution in India (from the 1960s) is known for high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds of wheat and rice, along with more fertilisers, pesticides and irrigation. It raised food grain production greatly.

subject: economics
text: Self Help Groups offer loan on _________________.
options: a rate more than bank rates
explanation: Self Help Groups (SHGs) give small loans to their members at a nominal (low) rate of interest, much lower than moneylenders charge.

subject: economics
text: Geeta needs to purchase some shoes, and she has an excess of wheat. Archna has surplus wheat, and she needs to purchase shoes. This situation can be termed as:
explanation: When each person has what the other wants, it is called a double coincidence of wants. This is needed in a barter system (exchange without money).

subject: economics
text: In India, how is the buffer stock used to address food security issues?
options: By distributing free food to all citizens
By providing subsidised grains through the Public Distribution System (PDS)
By selling surplus grains to private retailers
By exporting excess grain to other countries
explanation: The government stores buffer stock of wheat and rice through the FCI, and gives it out at subsidised prices through the Public Distribution System (PDS), which helps in food security.

subject: economics
text: Which of the following is true about Great Gatsby Curve?
options: It compares poverty levels between rural and urban populations.
It measures the correlation between poverty and literacy rates.
It illustrates the role of government subsidies in reducing poverty.
It demonstrates the link between inequality and income mobility (across generations).
explanation: The Great Gatsby Curve shows that countries with higher income inequality tend to have lower income mobility between generations. So children of poor parents find it harder to move up.

subject: economics
text: The concept of "Human Capital" in the context of population as a resource focuses primarily on:
explanation: Human capital means the skills, knowledge and health of people, which are built through education and training. So this concept focuses on educational and skill development.

subject: economics
text: Which of the following is NOT an indicator of an economically developed nation?
options: High levels of life expectancy at birth
Low levels of infant mortality rate
A high proportion of labour in the primary sector
explanation: Developed countries have high life expectancy, low infant mortality and high literacy. A high share of workers in the primary sector (agriculture) is a sign of an underdeveloped economy.

subject: economics
text: What is the aim of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan?
options: Provide elementary education for the urban poor children
Provide elementary education for all children in the age group 6-14 years
Provide elementary education for the rural poor
explanation: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA, 2001) aimed to provide free and compulsory elementary education to all children aged 6-14 years, in line with the Right to Education.

subject: economics
text: What is the primary objective of the Public Distribution System (PDS) in reducing inequality?
options: Ensuring food security and reducing hunger among the poor people
explanation: The Public Distribution System (PDS) gives food grains at low prices to poor families. This helps ensure food security, reduces hunger and lowers inequality.

subject: economics
text: What is the purpose of sustainable development goals (SDGs)?
options: To increase industrialisation at any cost
To balance economic growth, environmental sustainability and social equity
To focus solely on rural development
explanation: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) aim to balance economic growth, protection of the environment and social equity, so that the needs of the future generations are not harmed.

subject: economics
text: The most common feature of the SHG is _______________________.
explanation: Self Help Groups are small groups of people who save together and lend to one another. The main aim is social welfare and development of the members, not profit maximisation.

subject: economics
text: Who published the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023?
explanation: NITI Aayog publishes the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), with the 2023 report using data from NFHS-5. It looks at health, education and living standards.

subject: economics
text: Disinvestment of public sector enterprises (PSEs) implies which of the following?
options: Sale of equity shares to private / public sector
explanation: Disinvestment means the government sells part of its shares (equity) in a public sector enterprise to the public or private buyers. The government need not close the company.

subject: economics
text: ___________ is the benchmark currency measures, which is used for the money supply.
explanation: M1 (narrow money: currency with the public plus demand deposits) is the most liquid measure and is considered the benchmark measure of money supply.

subject: economics
text: How has the COVID-19 pandemic affected job opportunities in the industrial sector?
explanation: The COVID-19 pandemic caused lockdowns and shut factories, so many jobs were lost in the industrial sector.

subject: economics
text:
Which of the following statements regarding food security in India are correct?
1. Food security means ensuring that all people have physical, social and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food at all times.
2. The Public Distribution System (PDS) does not play any significant role in ensuring food security in India.
3. India's National Food Security Act (NFSA) 2013 ensures a legal right to food for 75% of the rural population.
4. The Green Revolution had no impact on India's food security.
explanation: Food security means access to enough, safe and nutritious food for all at all times (statement 1 is right). The NFSA 2013 covers up to 75% of the rural population (statement 3 is right). The PDS and Green Revolution had a major positive effect, so statements 2 and 4 are wrong.

subject: economics
text: What is the primary concept associated with the work of AGB Fisher and Colin Clark?
explanation: A.G.B. Fisher and Colin Clark gave the idea of sectoral shift, i.e. as an economy develops, workers and output move from the primary sector to the secondary and then the tertiary sector.

subject: economics
text: Which of the following is a policy recommendation to reduce poverty and inequality in India?
options: Increasing public investment in health and education
explanation: Investing more public money in health and education improves people's skills and opportunities, which reduces poverty and inequality. Cutting the minimum wage or taxing less on luxuries would increase inequality.

subject: economics
text: Who was the chief architect of the Second Five-Year Plan along with Jawaharlal Nehru?
explanation: P.C. Mahalanobis was the architect of the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61), which focused on rapid industrialisation, especially heavy industries.

subject: economics
text: Which of the following programmes is designed to provide vocational training and employment opportunities to rural youth in India?
options: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)
explanation: DDU-GKY (Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana) gives skill training and jobs to rural youth. MGNREGA gives wage work, NRHM is for health and APY is a pension scheme.

subject: economics
text: In which year did the Ministry of Education start the National Service Scheme?
explanation: The National Service Scheme (NSS) was started in 1969-70 (24 September 1969, Gandhiji's birth centenary year) by the Ministry of Education to involve students in community service.

subject: economics
text: Which of the following has been replaced by money as a medium of exchange in India?
explanation: Money replaced the barter system, in which goods were exchanged directly for goods. Money removed the need for the double coincidence of wants.

subject: economics
text: In which year was the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act passed?
explanation: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) was passed in 2005 and now is called MGNREGA. It guarantees 100 days of wage employment a year to rural households.

subject: economics
text: In which year was the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) started?
explanation: The Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) started in April 1999 to promote self-employment among the rural poor through Self Help Groups. It was later restructured as the National Rural Livelihood Mission.

subject: economics
text: What is the minimum stock of food grains maintained by the government for food security called?
explanation: Buffer stock is the stock of wheat and rice bought by the government (through FCI) and kept as a reserve for food security and to control prices.

subject: economics
text: Which type of unemployment arises due to economic recession and a decline in consumer demand?
explanation: Cyclical unemployment occurs during a recession or slowdown, when demand falls and firms cut down jobs. It goes away when the economy recovers.

subject: economics
text: Which of the following sectors is most associated with informal employment in developing countries?
explanation: Informal (unorganised) employment is mostly found in agriculture in developing countries like India, where the majority of workers are self-employed or casual labourers without job security.

subject: economics
text: What is the name of the flagship programme implemented by the Government of India that guarantees 100 days of paid employment per year to rural households?
options: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (PMGKRA)
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
explanation: MGNREGA (2005) guarantees 100 days of paid work per year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

subject: economics
text: Which of the following types of inflation cannot be controlled?
explanation: Hyperinflation is a very fast, extreme rise in prices (over 50% a month) that loses control and destroys the value of money. Creeping, walking and galloping inflation can be controlled by policy.

subject: economics
