explanation: To be recognised as a State Party, a party must win at least 6% of the valid votes in the state and at least 2 seats in the Legislative Assembly.

subject: political-science
text: Under Article 248 of the Constitution, the power to make any law with respect to any matter mentioned in the Concurrent List or the State List (residuary powers) vests in _____________.
explanation: Under Article 248, Parliament has the residuary powers, i.e. the power to make laws on subjects not in any of the three lists.

subject: political-science
text: Which event in 2006 marked the end of absolute monarchy and the beginning of democracy in Nepal?
explanation: In 2006, the Jan Andolan II (second people's movement) in Nepal ended the absolute rule of the king and began democracy.

subject: political-science
text: The right to vote in the elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies is based on the principle of 'universal adult suffrage', which is provided by _________.
explanation: Article 326 provides for elections on the basis of adult suffrage. Every citizen of 18 years or above can vote.

subject: political-science
text: Social differences that reinforce each other and create a sense of social division, making it difficult to reconcile groups, are called what?
explanation: When social differences (caste, religion, class) overlap and reinforce each other, they create deep divisions. These are called overlapping differences. Cross-cutting differences are easier to accommodate.

subject: political-science
text: In India, elections to the Rajya Sabha are conducted by which of the following methods?
options: Indirect election by the State Legislative Assemblies
explanation: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected indirectly by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies, using the single transferable vote system.

subject: political-science
text: Under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, who is the final deciding authority in the case of disqualification of a member of the Lok Sabha?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
explanation: Under the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha for Rajya Sabha) decides whether a member is disqualified.

subject: political-science
text: The challenge of 'identity politics' in democracies arises mainly due to what?
options: Politicisation of social and cultural identities
explanation: Identity politics arises when social and cultural identities like caste, religion and language are turned into political tools.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following is NOT an essential component of a political party?
explanation: A political party has an organisation, a common set of principles and works for the national interest through constitutional means. Distrust in constitutional means is not part of it.

subject: political-science
text: When voters choose candidates on the basis of performance and accountability rather than identity, which of the following does this indicate?
options: The maturity of democratic political culture and informed citizenship
The consolidation of authoritarian tendencies in electoral politics
Disconnection between leadership and civic representation
The decline of democratic values and political participation
explanation: When voters choose on the basis of performance and accountability, and not identity, it shows a mature democratic culture and informed citizens.

subject: political-science
text: What was the constitutional significance of the last session of the Constituent Assembly in January 1950?
options: It dissolved the Constituent Assembly and restored the colonial administration.
It signalled the beginning of a new political order based on constitutionalism.
It repealed the constitutions of all states and merged them under British control.
It marked the transfer of legislative powers to the Governor-General.
explanation: In January 1950 the Constituent Assembly's last session marked the start of a new political order based on constitutionalism, with the Constitution coming into force on 26 January 1950.

subject: political-science
text: Why were some provisions of the Indian Constitution, such as citizenship and elections, enforced before 26 January 1950?
options: To delay the introduction of democratic rights until elections were held
To restrict the operation of fundamental rights until the first Parliament met
To allow the Governor-General to continue the British administration smoothly
To enable preparation of democratic functioning before full implementation
explanation: Provisions on citizenship, elections and provisional Parliament came into force on 26 November 1949 itself, so that democratic institutions could be prepared before the full Constitution took effect on 26 January 1950.

subject: political-science
text: The 'Objectives Resolution' presented by Jawaharlal Nehru was important because ________.
options: it provided a guiding philosophy for the making of the Indian Constitution
it declared India a dominion under the Crown of England
it limited the powers of the Constituent Assembly to administrative matters
it proposed the immediate implementation of the British constitutional framework
explanation: Nehru's Objectives Resolution (1946) gave the guiding philosophy for making the Constitution: sovereignty of the people, justice, liberty and equality. It did not make India a dominion or copy the British framework.

subject: political-science
text: Which was declared the law of the land after the adoption of the Constitution?
explanation: After it was adopted, the Constitution became the supreme law (law of the land) of India. All institutions, including Parliament and the President, must follow it.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following best describes the significance of the composition of the Constituent Assembly in ensuring democratic legitimacy?
options: It included members from various provinces, communities and political groups.
It was entirely dominated by representatives of the princely states.
It represented only the leaders of the Indian National Congress.
It included only members nominated by the British Government.
explanation: The Constituent Assembly included members from different provinces, communities and political groups, which gave the Constitution democratic legitimacy. It was not only Congress or British nominees.

subject: political-science
text: What does the 'adoption' of the Indian Constitution by the Constituent Assembly mainly represent?
options: Immediate implementation of all provisions without any delay
The beginning of the drafting of a new document for administrative purposes
Suspension of all previous legal systems until the creation of the new code
The formal acceptance of the Constitution as the supreme law of the country
explanation: The adoption (26 November 1949) was the formal acceptance of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly as the supreme law. Only some provisions came into force at once and the rest on 26 January 1950.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following statements best explains why the Indian Constitution was formally adopted on 26 November 1949?
options: This date symbolises the culmination of India's long struggle for independence and self-rule.
This date marked the first session of the British Parliament on India's independence.
This date was chosen because it was the anniversary of the Quit India Movement.
The date was chosen to be in line with the UN Charter on democracy.
explanation: 26 November 1949 is the day the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution, marking the culmination of India's struggle for self-rule. It is now celebrated as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas).

subject: political-science
text: Subhash Kashyap argues that the real power of Parliament lies in ________.
options: its direct control over the appointment of judges and bureaucrats
its power to issue binding judicial interpretations of constitutional articles
its capacity to publicly debate, question and hold the executive accountable
its authority to enforce judicial decisions and executive orders
explanation: Subhash Kashyap, a constitutional expert, said the real power of Parliament lies in its ability to debate, question and hold the executive accountable, and not in appointing judges or interpreting the law.

subject: political-science
text: Who popularised the concept of 'illiberal democracy'?
explanation: Fareed Zakaria popularised the term 'illiberal democracy' (1997) for countries that hold elections but do not protect civil liberties and the rule of law.

subject: political-science
text: In which of the following international bodies does India play a leading role to promote regional cooperation in South Asia?
explanation: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, 1985) is a regional group of South Asian countries, in which India plays a leading role. G20, ASEAN and the EU are not South Asian bodies.

subject: political-science
text: Who was the political thinker who, while describing democracy, called the people "a certain number of millions, mostly fools"?
explanation: The Scottish writer Thomas Carlyle, a critic of democracy, described the people as 'thirty millions, mostly fools'.

subject: political-science
text: What does the Indian constitutional ideal of a 'secular state' mean?
options: The state gives priority to the majority religion
The state has its own religion
The state has no religion of its own
explanation: A secular state has no official religion of its own, and treats all religions equally. It is not anti-religion.

subject: political-science
text: Within how many days from the date of its formation must an application for the registration of a political party be submitted to the Election Commission?
explanation: An application for registration of a political party must be sent to the Election Commission within 30 days of the party's formation, under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

subject: political-science
text: Which form of democracy is most widely practised in the contemporary world?
explanation: Representative democracy, in which people elect representatives to make decisions, is the most common form of democracy in the world, because direct democracy is not possible in large countries.

subject: political-science
text: Under which Article can the Rajya Sabha declare that it is necessary in the national interest for Parliament to make laws on a subject in the State List?
explanation: Under Article 249, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution with a two-thirds majority that it is in the national interest, Parliament can make laws on a State List subject.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following does NOT analyse the negative role of caste in Indian politics?
options: Basis of formation and identity of political parties
Leaders finding a ready-made organisation in the form of caste for attaining power
Promotion of regionalism and regional parties
Different forms of caste existing in different states
explanation: The negative role of caste in politics covers caste-based parties, leaders using caste organisations to win power and caste feeding regionalism. The fact that caste has different forms in different states is just a description and not a negative role.

subject: political-science
text: According to the Indian Constitution, all doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of the President or Vice-President of India shall be inquired into and decided by __________ only.
options: a special tribunal appointed by the Chief Justice
explanation: Under Article 71, all doubts and disputes about the election of the President or Vice-President are decided only by the Supreme Court.

subject: political-science
text: Jeffery Webber argues that the core contradiction of the Morales era was ________________.
options: complete withdrawal from global trade regimes
explanation: Jeffery Webber argues that in Bolivia under Evo Morales, the state spoke of a plurinational and indigenous-friendly vision but continued the extraction of natural resources like gas and minerals, which was the core contradiction.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following activities is NOT a part of political participation?
options: Official membership of a political party
explanation: Voting, joining a party and campaigning are forms of political participation. Staying away from elections is the opposite of it.

subject: political-science
text: 'The Indian Constitution is neither purely unitary nor purely federal, but a combination of both.' Which scholar made this statement?
explanation: D.D. Basu described the Indian Constitution as neither purely unitary nor purely federal, but a combination of both. K.C. Wheare called it quasi-federal.

subject: political-science
text: Who first presented the concept of Directed Democracy?
explanation: Sukarno of Indonesia put forward the idea of 'Guided (Directed) Democracy' in the late 1950s, in which the leader guided the decisions instead of full party competition.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following is the accurate explanation of regionalism in a vast and diverse country?
options: A group's desire for development and recognition of its distinct identity
A movement based only on claiming new states
A political ideology followed only by a minority group
An anti-national activity that always leads to separatism
explanation: Regionalism is a group's desire for development and for recognition of its distinct identity. It is not always anti-national or separatist.

subject: political-science
text: Democratic governments develop mechanisms to resolve differences and reduce the possibility of social tension. Which of the following mechanisms in India is an example of such a mechanism?
options: Reservation policy for socially and educationally backward classes
explanation: Reservation for socially and educationally backward classes is a democratic way to reduce inequality and social tension. Abolishing languages or a one-party system would not.

subject: political-science
text: What is the full form of the INDIA alliance?
explanation: INDIA stands for 'Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance', the alliance of opposition parties formed in 2023.

subject: political-science
text: What is participatory democracy?
options: Only the elites decide national policies.
Citizens are actively involved in political processes and decision-making.
Political parties control all government functions.
explanation: In participatory democracy, citizens actively take part in political processes and decision-making, instead of only voting.

subject: political-science
text: The concept 'Power means the ability to produce the desired effect' is attributed to which thinker?
explanation: Bertrand Russell defined power as 'the production of intended effects', i.e. the ability to produce the desired effect.

subject: political-science
text: The executive head of a Municipal Corporation is the __________.
explanation: The Municipal Commissioner is the chief executive of a Municipal Corporation. The Mayor is the elected head who presides over meetings.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following thinkers was an opponent of democracy?
explanation: Plato was a critic of democracy. He preferred the rule of philosopher-kings, as he thought that ordinary people were not wise enough to rule.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following situations best illustrates the concept of a 'level playing field' in elections?
options: Equal access to media and financial resources for all electoral parties
Permission for advertisements by the ruling party on polling days
Licence to launch government schemes during elections
Ban on opposition rallies to ensure peace and order
explanation: A 'level playing field' means all parties get equal opportunities, like equal access to the media and money. Advantages for the ruling party or bans on the opposition would defeat this.

subject: political-science
text: Under which Article has the Indian Constitution provided advisory jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of India?
explanation: Article 143 gives the President the power to seek the advice of the Supreme Court on questions of law or fact. This is the Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction.

subject: political-science
text: The Right to Constitutional Remedies is considered the 'heart and soul' of the Indian Constitution because it _____.
options: empowers the Election Commission to conduct free elections
enables Parliament to amend any part of the Constitution
gives citizens the power to approach the courts for the enforcement of rights
enables the President to suspend rights during an emergency
explanation: Dr Ambedkar called the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution because it lets citizens go to the courts to enforce their rights.

subject: political-science
text: How many members were there originally in the Constituent Assembly?
explanation: The Constituent Assembly originally had 389 members: 292 from British provinces, 4 from chief commissioner provinces and 93 from princely states. It reduced to 299 after Partition.

subject: political-science
text: In which case did the Supreme Court of India propound the concept of the basic structure of the Indian Constitution?
options: S. R. Bommai v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
explanation: The basic structure doctrine was laid down in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973). The Court held that Parliament cannot change the basic features of the Constitution.

subject: political-science
text: Who has been designated as the protector of Fundamental Rights under the Indian Constitution?
explanation: The Supreme Court is the protector (guardian) of Fundamental Rights, and can issue writs under Article 32.

subject: political-science
text: The judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) is significant because it _____________.
options: declared the President the final interpreter of fundamental rights
allowed Parliament to amend the Constitution without any restriction
applied the basic structure doctrine, thereby limiting Parliament's power of amendment
established that fundamental rights can be permanently suspended
explanation: In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), the Supreme Court said Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot destroy its basic structure.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental feature of a democratic system?
explanation: Independent judiciary, free elections and freedom of speech are features of democracy. Rule by a single party is not, as it removes competition.

subject: political-science
text: Which feature of the functioning of the Constituent Assembly reflects its democratic spirit?
options: Refusing to consider any suggestion of minority representatives
Decision-making through extensive discussion and consensus-building
Drafting by a selected group of British legal experts only
Adopting the Constitution without any debate or amendment
explanation: The Constituent Assembly showed democratic spirit by discussing everything at length and taking decisions by consensus, over nearly three years.

subject: political-science
text: When the Supreme Court strikes down a law passed by Parliament as unconstitutional, which of the following functions does it perform?
options: Original jurisdiction over disputes between citizens
explanation: When the Supreme Court strikes down a law as unconstitutional, it is exercising judicial review, which keeps the Constitution supreme.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following is NOT a reason for social differences due to the accident of birth?
explanation: Social differences based on accident of birth include height, gender and colour. Economic status (rich-poor) can change over time, so it is not solely an accident of birth.

subject: political-science
text: Which among the following countries demonstrates power sharing through coalition governments?
explanation: Germany has coalition governments, where no single party gets a majority, so parties share power. This is an example of power sharing among parties.

subject: political-science
text: The People’s Movement (Jana Andolan) in Nepal in 2006 primarily resulted in the:
options: abolition of monarchy and the establishment of a republic
partition of the country into autonomous zones
explanation: The 2006 Jana Andolan in Nepal ended the king's rule and led to the abolition of the monarchy and the setting up of a republic (declared in 2008).

subject: political-science
text: The Delimitation Commission in India functions under:
options: Article 82 of the Constitution and the Delimitation Act
explanation: The Delimitation Commission draws the boundaries of constituencies. It works under Article 82 and the Delimitation Act, and its orders cannot be challenged in court.

subject: political-science
text: The concept of 'intersectionality' — crucial to understanding democracy and diversity — was first introduced by:
explanation: Kimberle Crenshaw introduced the term 'intersectionality' (1989) to describe how overlapping identities like race and gender produce different experiences of discrimination.

subject: political-science
text: Which historical document limited the powers of the king and laid the foundation for constitutional governance?
explanation: The Magna Carta (1215) limited the powers of the English king and laid the foundation for constitutional government.

subject: political-science
text: Which pillar means the division of government powers into separate branches?
explanation: Separation of powers divides government power between separate branches: legislature, executive and judiciary. Checks and balances is how they limit each other.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following movements best exemplifies the democratic accommodation of ethnic diversity through federal restructuring?
explanation: The Telangana movement resulted in the creation of a separate state (2014) within the Indian federation, an example of accommodating regional identity by restructuring states.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following is an example of a substantive feature of democracy?
explanation: Substantive features of democracy are the real freedoms and rights, like freedom of speech and expression. Holding elections and sessions are procedural features.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following is true regarding the Anti-Defection Law in India?
options: Applicable only to the Rajya Sabha
Introduced through the 52nd Amendment, 1985, as the Tenth Schedule
explanation: The anti-defection law came through the 52nd Amendment (1985) and is the Tenth Schedule. It is applicable to both Houses of Parliament and state legislatures.

subject: political-science
text: The Kuldip Nayar vs. Union of India (2006) case upheld:
options: open ballot system for Rajya Sabha elections
explanation: In Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2006), the Supreme Court upheld the open ballot system in Rajya Sabha elections to prevent cross-voting and corruption.

subject: political-science
text: The term 'Cadre-based party' refers to:
options: a party organised around professional politicians
a party built on disciplined membership and ideological commitment
a party dependent on mass media campaigns
a party led by a single charismatic leader
explanation: A cadre-based party is built on a small but disciplined membership with a strong ideology and commitment (e.g. communist parties). A mass-based party is open to all.

subject: political-science
text: Which best describes Majoritarianism?
options: Governance based on consensus among groups
Equal representation of all social groups
Domination of the majority community in decision-making
Sharing power among different social groups
explanation: Majoritarianism means that the majority community dominates the decision-making, and the interests of minorities are ignored.

subject: political-science
text: In democratic societies, managing diversity involves:
options: ensuring representation, dialogue and mutual respect
explanation: Managing diversity in a democracy means ensuring representation, dialogue and mutual respect. Suppressing cultures or imposing uniformity increases conflict.

subject: political-science
text: The Tarkunde Committee (1975) is associated with:
explanation: The Tarkunde Committee (1974-75), set up by Jayaprakash Narayan, suggested electoral reforms such as a multi-member Election Commission.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following thinkers argued that democracy must ensure 'recognition' as well as 'redistribution'?
explanation: Nancy Fraser argued that justice needs both recognition (of identity and culture) and redistribution (of wealth and resources).

subject: political-science
text: Which city is considered the birthplace of democracy?
explanation: Athens in ancient Greece is regarded as the birthplace of democracy, where citizens took part directly in decision-making.

subject: political-science
text: Maurice Duverger’s 'law' establishes a relationship between:
options: electoral systems and the number of political parties
explanation: Duverger's Law says that the FPTP (plurality) system tends to produce a two-party system, and proportional representation supports many parties. So it links electoral systems with the number of parties.

subject: political-science
text: The Indrajit Gupta Committee Report (1998) emphasised that:
options: partial state funding was desirable, conditional on transparency
total state funding of elections was feasible
election expenses should be borne by candidates
only national parties should get public funds
explanation: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) supported partial state funding of elections, for recognised parties, along with transparency in accounts.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
explanation: The Drafting Committee had Dr Ambedkar (chair), K.M. Munshi, Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Saiyid Muhammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rao and T.T. Krishnamachari. Dr Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Assembly, not a member of it.

subject: political-science
text: From where did the Constituent Assembly of India derive its authority to frame the Constitution?
options: A direct general election held for the purpose
explanation: The Constituent Assembly claimed its authority from the people of India, though it was elected indirectly by the provincial assemblies. It was not created by a direct general election.

subject: political-science
text: No citizen shall face discrimination while entering shops, public places, restaurants, hotels or any Public Place. This rule is given under which Article of the Indian Constitution?
explanation: Article 15(2) says that no citizen can be denied access to shops, public restaurants, hotels and places of public entertainment on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

subject: political-science
text: When was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly for framing the Indian Constitution convened?
explanation: The Constituent Assembly of India met for the first time on 9 December 1946 in New Delhi, and Dr Sachchidananda Sinha was its temporary president.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following is NOT a concern of procedural democracy?
options: Civil liberties like freedom of speech
explanation: Procedural democracy is concerned with the rules and process: adult suffrage, regular elections and civil liberties. Socio-economic equality is a concern of substantive democracy.

subject: political-science
text: Which prominent constitutional expert made the critical observation that the Indian Constitution was a lawyer's paradise?
explanation: Sir Ivor Jennings, a British constitutional expert, called the Indian Constitution a 'lawyer's paradise' because of its length and complexity.

subject: political-science
text: What is the maximum time, as per the Constitution, to conduct the election of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha after the first sitting?
options: There is no maximum time specified.
explanation: The Constitution says that the Lok Sabha shall choose the Speaker 'as soon as may be' after its first sitting, without a set time limit.

subject: political-science
text: What was the status of India on 25 November 1949?
explanation: On 25 November 1949 India was still a Dominion. It became a republic on 26 January 1950 when the Constitution came into force.

subject: political-science
text: The term 'consociational democracy' — used to explain power-sharing in deeply divided societies — was introduced by:
explanation: The term 'consociational democracy' was brought in by the political scientist Arend Lijphart to describe power sharing in deeply divided societies.

subject: political-science
text: The power-sharing arrangement in Belgium is an example of which model?
explanation: Belgium shares power between its language communities (Dutch, French, German) and the regions, which is a consociational model.

subject: political-science
text: The Global State of Democracy Report is published by:
options: International IDEA (Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance)
explanation: The Global State of Democracy Report is published by International IDEA (Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance), based in Stockholm.

subject: political-science
text: The primary cause of declining voter turnout in advanced democracies, according to Robert Putnam, is:
options: decline in social capital and civic engagement
explanation: Robert Putnam argued that the fall in social capital and civic engagement (people joining fewer groups and associations) reduces political participation.

subject: political-science
text: Robert A Dahl’s concept of Polyarchy refers to:
options: a military rule under popular control
a practical form of democracy with competition and participation
explanation: Robert Dahl used 'polyarchy' for a real-world (practical) form of democracy with competition among parties and participation of citizens.

subject: political-science
text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the distribution of legislative powers between the Centre and the States?
explanation: Article 246 divides legislative powers between the Union and the States. It refers to the Union, State and Concurrent Lists of the Seventh Schedule.

subject: political-science
text: Which challenge is most fundamental when a non-democratic State moves towards democracy?
explanation: The 'foundational challenge' is the first challenge that a non-democratic country faces when moving to democracy: making the transition and setting up a democratic government.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following scholars proposed the concept of 'cartel party,' where parties collude with the state to maintain dominance?
explanation: Richard Katz and Peter Mair proposed the 'cartel party' theory, in which major parties share state resources and work together to protect their own position.

subject: political-science
text: Who has the power to disqualify a candidate or member on the grounds of defection?
options: Speaker or Chairman of the legislature
explanation: Under the Tenth Schedule, the Speaker (Lok Sabha) or Chairman (Rajya Sabha) decides disqualification of a member for defection.

subject: political-science
text: The concept of 'proportional representation by means of single transferable vote' is used in India for electing:
explanation: Rajya Sabha members are elected by proportional representation through the single transferable vote (STV) method by the state legislators.

subject: political-science
text: India's foreign policy aims to promote which of the following values?
explanation: India's foreign policy is based on non-violence, peace and Panchsheel (peaceful coexistence), and it does not seek dominance.

subject: political-science
text: National Voters' Day is celebrated on:
explanation: National Voters' Day is celebrated on 25 January every year, since the Election Commission of India was founded on that day in 1950.

subject: political-science
text: Iris Marion Young’s idea of 'politics of difference' implies that:
options: all citizens should be treated identically
differences should be recognised and valued within democratic decision-making
explanation: Iris Marion Young's 'politics of difference' means that differences among groups should be recognised and valued in democratic decision-making, and not ignored.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following thinkers emphasised the danger of 'tyranny of the majority' in democracies?
explanation: Alexis de Tocqueville, in 'Democracy in America', warned of the 'tyranny of the majority', where the majority may trample on the rights of the minority. J.S. Mill also wrote about it, but Tocqueville is most linked with the phrase.

subject: political-science
text: State party recognition requires:
options: 6% vote share in the state + 2 Assembly seats or 1 Lok Sabha seat
explanation: To be recognised as a State Party, a party needs at least 6% of valid votes in the state, along with 2 Assembly seats (or 1 Lok Sabha seat), as per the Election Commission's rules.

subject: political-science
text: Which international organisation has equal voting rights to its members without any special power given to any group of countries?
explanation: In the UN General Assembly every member country has one vote, and no country has special powers. In the Security Council, five permanent members have veto power, and in the World Bank and IMF votes depend on the money contributed.

subject: political-science
text: Power sharing among different levels of government is called:
options: allocation of resources to different states
division of powers among legislature, executive, and judiciary
explanation: Sharing power between different levels of government, like the Union and the states, is the federal (vertical) division of power. Division among the legislature, executive and judiciary is horizontal.

subject: political-science
text: The Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 empowers which institution to recognise political parties in India?
explanation: The Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, lets the Election Commission of India recognise parties as national or state parties and allot symbols to them.

subject: political-science
text: The Inter-State Council was set up under which Article of the Indian Constitution?
explanation: Article 263 provides for the establishment of an Inter-State Council to help coordination between the states and the Centre. It was set up in 1990.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following scenarios best constitutes a violation of the Right to Life and Personal Liberty under Article 21?
options: A person is placed under preventive detention after approval from the court.
The government acquires land for public purposes after compensating the landowner.
The government issues an arrest warrant without following legal procedures.
A person is arrested for a crime with a valid arrest warrant and legal representation
explanation: Article 21 says life and liberty can be taken away only by a procedure established by law. Arresting someone without following legal procedure violates this. The other options follow legal procedure.

subject: political-science
text: How many Parts and Schedules were there in the original Constitution of India as adopted in 1950?
explanation: The original Constitution had 395 Articles in 22 Parts and 8 Schedules. Now it has more Parts and 12 Schedules due to amendments.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following statements is true?
options: Procedural democracy automatically ensures social and economic justice.
Procedural democracy guarantees equality in outcomes.
Substantive democracy focuses on outcomes and social justice.
explanation: Procedural democracy is about the rules and process (like elections). Substantive democracy focuses on real outcomes, like social justice and equality.

subject: political-science
text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to vote to all citizens who have attained the age of 18 years?
explanation: Article 326 says elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies are held on the basis of adult suffrage. The voting age was lowered to 18 by the 61st Amendment (1988).

subject: political-science
text: At the time of adoption of the Constitution, how many categories of Fundamental Rights were included in Part III?
explanation: Originally the Constitution had seven categories of Fundamental Rights, including the Right to Property. It was removed by the 44th Amendment (1978), leaving six.

subject: political-science
text: On which date is Law Day observed in India?
explanation: Law Day (Samvidhan Diwas) is observed on 26 November, the day the Constitution was adopted in 1949.

subject: political-science
text: 'Democracy is government of the people, by the people and for the people', is a famous quote by:
explanation: Abraham Lincoln, in his Gettysburg Address (1863), defined democracy as 'government of the people, by the people, for the people'.

subject: political-science
text: Which Article provides for the election of a type of local body?
explanation: Article 243ZA (74th Amendment) provides for the election of Municipalities. 243K is for Panchayats' elections.

subject: political-science
text: Arrange the following events related to the Maoist movement in Nepal in chronological ascending order. The initiation of the armed insurgency by the Maoists. The signing of the peace agreement between the Maoists and the government. The establishment of the interim government. The declaration of a federal democratic republic in Nepal.
explanation: In Nepal, the Maoist insurgency began in 1996, the peace agreement was signed in 2006, the interim government was formed in 2007 and the federal democratic republic was declared in 2008.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following best exemplifies 'procedural' democracy rather than 'substantive' democracy?
options: Regular free and fair elections with protection of minority rights
Elections are held regularly due to media control, but there is a lack of real choice
An independent judiciary that ensures the rule of law
explanation: Procedural democracy has the outward forms of democracy (like elections) but lacks real choice. A state that controls the media and holds regular elections, but gives no real choice, shows this.

subject: political-science
text: Under which Article does the Indian Constitution direct the State to organise village Panchayats?
explanation: Article 40 (Directive Principles) says the State should organise village panchayats and give them powers to work as units of self-government.

subject: political-science
text: Which country’s Constitution reflects majoritarian principles?
explanation: Sri Lanka's constitution reflected majoritarianism, as Sinhala was made the only official language in 1956 and Buddhism was given a special place, which led to conflict with Tamils.

subject: political-science
text: According to Amartya Sen, identities in a democracy should be understood as:
explanation: Amartya Sen argues that a person has many identities (like religion, class, gender, profession) and which one matters depends on the context. Identity is not fixed or singular.

subject: political-science
text: Who described the Indian Constitution as 'quasi-federal'?
explanation: K.C. Wheare described the Indian Constitution as 'quasi-federal' (federal in form but with a unitary tilt).

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following is an indirect election?
options: Election of members of the Rajya Sabha
Election of members of the State Legislative Assembly
Election of members of the Lok Sabha
explanation: In an indirect election, people elect representatives, who then elect others. Rajya Sabha members are elected by MLAs. The Lok Sabha and Assembly members are directly elected by people.

subject: political-science
text: Which digital platform played an important role in organising the Generation Z-led protests in Nepal in 2025?
explanation: In the Gen Z protests in Nepal in September 2025, young people used digital platforms to organise, and Discord was used to discuss and choose an interim leader.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following best exemplifies how checks and balances function in a democratic system?
options: The judiciary has the power to nullify laws that violate the constitution.
The legislative branch enforces the laws passed by the executive.
The president can override decisions made by the judicial system.
The executive branch makes laws and also ensures they are enforced.
explanation: Checks and balances mean each organ can limit the others. When the judiciary strikes down a law that violates the Constitution, it checks the legislature.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following countries provides an example of ethnic power-sharing arrangement through the Dayton Agreement (1995)?
explanation: The Dayton Agreement (1995) ended the Bosnian war and set up ethnic power sharing between Bosniaks, Croats and Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

subject: political-science
text: Community government in Belgium is an example of power sharing among _________.
explanation: In Belgium, community government is elected by people of one language (Dutch, French and German-speaking). It handles cultural, educational and language matters. So power is shared among linguistic communities.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following is an example of horizontal power sharing?
options: Power sharing between Flemings and Walloons in Belgium
Division of powers between the Union and State in India
Division of powers among the legislature, executive, and judiciary
Allocation of resources to different states
explanation: Horizontal power sharing is the division of power among the organs of government at the same level: legislature, executive and judiciary.

subject: political-science
text: What is the intermediate-level Panchayati Raj institution called?
explanation: The three tiers of Panchayati Raj are the Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block, the intermediate level) and Zila Parishad (district).

subject: political-science
text: Bolivia’s 'Water War' (Cochabamba, 2000) is significant because:
options: it initiated a coup against the government
it was a struggle against privatisation of essential services
it led to military occupation of the city
explanation: The Cochabamba 'Water War' (2000) in Bolivia was a mass protest against the privatisation of the city's water supply, which had raised water bills. The government cancelled the contract.

subject: political-science
text: The Bolivian and Nepalese cases both exemplify the concept of:
options: 'Revolutionary democracy' where violence is the only path to change
explanation: Both the Nepalese and Bolivian movements were 'contentious politics', where people used protests and pressure to change decisions and structures of the state.

subject: political-science
text: Which state constituted the Rajamannar Committee (1969), and what was its main recommendation?
options: Tamil Nadu - maximum financial and legislative autonomy to the states
explanation: The Tamil Nadu government set up the Rajamannar Committee (1969) which recommended more financial and legislative powers for the states.

subject: political-science
text: What does the word 'Kratia' mean in the Greek word 'Demokratia'?
explanation: 'Demokratia' comes from 'demos' (people) and 'kratia' (rule), so democracy means 'rule by the people'.

subject: political-science
text: How long did it take the Constituent Assembly to finalise the Constitution of India?
explanation: The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to complete the Constitution (from 9 December 1946 to 26 November 1949).

subject: political-science
text:
By whom is the Vice-President of India elected?
1. All members of Parliament (both elected and nominated)
2. Only elected members of Parliament
3. Members of the State Legislative Assemblies
4. Both MPs and MLAs as an electoral college
explanation: The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of all members of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, including nominated members). State legislators do not vote, unlike in the President's election.

subject: political-science
text: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution do citizens have the right to form associations, unions or co-operative societies?
explanation: Article 19(1)(c) gives citizens the right to form associations, unions or cooperative societies, and is a part of the Right to Freedom.

subject: political-science
text: If one session of the Parliament ends on 25 August 2026, what is the approximate latest date by which the next session must be held as per the Constitution of India?
explanation: The Constitution (Article 85) says that six months should not pass between two sessions of Parliament. So after 25 August 2026, the next session must be held by about 25 February 2027.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following individuals was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
explanation: The Drafting Committee had Ambedkar (Chairman), N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer, K.M. Munshi, Saadulla, N. Madhava Rao and T.T. Krishnamachari. Ravi Shankar Shukla was not a member.

subject: political-science
text: In the original Constitution of 1950, what was the subject matter of Part VII?
options: The States in Part B of the First Schedule
The States in Part A of the First Schedule
explanation: In the original Constitution, Part VII dealt with the States in Part B of the First Schedule. It was removed in 1956 by the Seventh Amendment.

subject: political-science
text: Which Schedule of the original Indian Constitution related to the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha?
explanation: The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution allots seats in the Rajya Sabha to the states and Union Territories.

subject: political-science
text: When was the last meeting of the Constituent Assembly held?
explanation: The last (twelfth) session of the Constituent Assembly met on 24 January 1950, when members signed the Constitution and Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected the first President.

subject: political-science
text: The movements in Nepal and Bolivia share which common characteristic?
options: Both movements sought to overthrow colonial governments.
Both revolutions were largely peaceful and aimed at securing democratic governance.
They were both led by military groups.
They were both driven by demands for greater economic liberalisation.
explanation: The movements in Nepal (2006) and Bolivia (2000-05) were mostly peaceful mass movements that aimed to secure democratic governance and rights for people.

subject: political-science
text: The word ‘democracy’ is a transliteration of the Greek word:
explanation: The word 'democracy' comes from the Greek word 'demokratia'.

subject: political-science
text: Direct democracy is characterised by which of the following?
options: A single political party controlling the state
Elected officials making decisions on behalf of the people
Citizens voting on every government decision
explanation: In a direct democracy, citizens vote on every government decision themselves. In a representative democracy, elected officials decide.

subject: political-science
text: One prudential reason for power sharing is that it:
options: strengthens the unchecked authority of the state
explanation: A 'prudential' reason for power sharing is a practical benefit. Power sharing reduces the chance of conflict between social groups and so keeps the country stable.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following best exemplifies vertical power sharing?
explanation: Vertical power sharing is the sharing of power among different levels of government. Panchayati Raj institutions (local governments) share power with the state government, so they exemplify it.

subject: political-science
text: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) in India?
explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions (1992, in force 1993). The 74th is for urban local bodies.

subject: political-science
text: What was the primary goal of the Jana Andolan (People’s Movement) in Nepal, which took place in 2006?
options: To restore democracy and end the monarchy’s absolute power
To secede from Nepal and form an independent state
explanation: The 2006 Jana Andolan in Nepal aimed to restore democracy and end the king's absolute power. It was a mass movement led by the Seven Party Alliance and the Maoists.

subject: political-science
text: Federalism in India ensures that power is shared between:
options: Local bodies and the Election Commission
Judiciary and Legislature at the Union level
the President and the Prime Minister equally
Central and State governments according to the Constitution
explanation: Federalism in India shares power between the Centre and the States, as laid down in the Constitution's lists (Union, State, Concurrent).

subject: political-science
text: Which pair correctly distinguishes horizontal from vertical power sharing?
options: Horizontal: among communities / Vertical: among different levels of government
Horizontal: among organs of government / Vertical: among levels of government
Horizontal: among levels of government / Vertical: among parties
Horizontal: among cities / Vertical: among organs
explanation: Horizontal power sharing is among the organs of government (legislature, executive, judiciary). Vertical power sharing is among different levels of government (Union, state, local).

subject: political-science
text: Which authority in India grants recognition and election symbols to political parties?
explanation: The Election Commission of India recognises political parties (national or state) and allots them election symbols.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following is a key feature of federalism?
explanation: A key feature of federalism is the division of powers between the central and state governments. A unitary or single-tier system is the opposite.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following should NOT be a feature of an electoral democracy?
options: Elections must offer the people a choice and a fair opportunity to change the current rulers.
Through elections, the government should be given full power to govern or amend the Constitution and the rights of citizens.
This choice and opportunity must be available to all people on an equal basis.
The rulers elected by the people must take all the major decisions.
explanation: In an electoral democracy, the government is elected by the people but cannot have unlimited power to change the Constitution or take away the rights of citizens. The government must work within the limits of the constitution.

subject: political-science
text: What does a 'Three-line Whip' mean?
options: Attendance and voting according to party directions are mandatory
Attendance is required, but voting is free
explanation: A three-line whip is an order from a party to its members to be present and to vote as the party directs. Not following it can lead to disciplinary action.

subject: political-science
text: The Preamble to the Indian Constitution secures to all its citizens' 'liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship'. This is the key provision for:
explanation: The Preamble's promise of liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship allows people of different religions and cultures to live together, so it helps in accommodating diversity.

subject: political-science
text: What legal measure did the Bolivian Government pass in 1999 to facilitate water privatisation?
explanation: In 1999 the Bolivian government passed Law 2029 (the Water Supply and Sanitation Law), which allowed the privatisation of water services, and this led to the Cochabamba Water War.

subject: political-science
text: In the Indian context, which Article of the Constitution provides for power sharing between Union and State legislatures?
explanation: Article 246 divides the legislative powers between Parliament and the state legislatures through the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.

subject: political-science
text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution describes India, that is, Bharat, as a 'Union of States' rather than a 'Federation of States'?
explanation: Article 1 says 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States'. Dr Ambedkar explained that the states cannot secede, so it is not a 'federation' by the agreement of states.

subject: political-science
text: Which element is considered most crucial for the stability of Indian democracy?
options: The proper functioning of independent judiciary and constitutional institutions
Personal leadership of the Prime Minister
explanation: The stability of Indian democracy depends most on the proper working of an independent judiciary and other constitutional institutions, which keep a check on power.

subject: political-science
text: Rights mentioned in which of the following Articles CANNOT be suspended even during emergency?
explanation: Articles 20 (protection in respect of conviction for offences) and 21 (right to life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency, as per the 44th Amendment (1978).

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following provisions of the Indian Constitution came into effect immediately after its adoption on 26 November 1949?
explanation: When the Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949, only some provisions, such as citizenship, elections and the provisional Parliament, came into force at once. The rest came into effect on 26 January 1950.

subject: political-science
text: Which case linked Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles, emphasising harmony?
options: AK Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
explanation: In Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980), the Supreme Court said the Constitution is founded on a balance (harmony) between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.

subject: political-science
text: In Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985), the Supreme Court held that:
options: Right to equality cannot be challenged
Parliament can suspend all rights during emergency
Right to livelihood is part of Article 21
explanation: In Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985), the Supreme Court held that the right to livelihood is part of the right to life under Article 21, in a case about pavement dwellers.

subject: political-science
text: Which Parliamentary committee examines demands for grants of ministries?
explanation: The Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) examine the demands for grants of ministries, and also study bills and annual reports.

subject: political-science
text: Which case clarified that the government must send back Collegium recommendations only once?
options: SP Gupta v. Union of India (1981)
Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (1998) – Third Judges Case
explanation: In the Third Judges Case (1998) the Supreme Court said that if the Collegium repeats its recommendation, the government must appoint, which means the government can send a name back only once.

subject: political-science
text: Which Article provides that laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void?
explanation: Article 13 says that any law that goes against the Fundamental Rights is void (invalid). This gives the courts the power of judicial review.

subject: political-science
text: Which of the following committees is NOT related to electoral reforms in India?
explanation: The Dinesh Goswami, T.N. Seshan and K. Santhanam committees were linked to electoral or political reforms. The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) was about Panchayati Raj.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: The Herbartian approach is based on the:
explanation: The Herbartian approach (Johann Herbart) is built around the presentation of content in steps: preparation, presentation, association, generalisation and application. It is teacher-led and content-focused.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following is a type of constructivism?
explanation: Constructivism has types like radical, social and cognitive constructivism. Radical constructivism (von Glasersfeld) says that each learner builds knowledge in their own mind. Emotional, value-based and philosophical are not types.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: _______ will NOT be considered a pedagogic practice focusing on the process of constructing knowledge.
explanation: Contextualised learning, reflective diaries and think-pair-share make students build knowledge actively. A lecture only transfers knowledge from teacher to student, so it is not a constructing practice.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following teaching-learning strategy is the most appropriate to facilitate secondary level learners to learn about the 'effect of the monsoon on crop production in India'?
explanation: For a topic like 'effect of monsoon on crop production', students should collect data, observe and analyse by themselves, so a project is best. A lecture or demonstration would only give ready-made facts.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following activities is NOT suitable for addressing the concerns of gender issue in curriculums?
options: In all experiments and projects, engage both boys and girls.
Themes related to chemical reactions and equations may include home-based examples such as preparation of pickles, jams, etc.
Importance of male members of the society needs to be highlighted in the discussion on themes such as natural resources, heredity and evolution, and our environment.
Give examples of women scientists wherever relevant in themes where women have contributed.
explanation: Stressing the importance of male members in themes such as natural resources or evolution would reinforce gender bias. Gender-sensitive teaching gives boys and girls equal roles, real-life examples and women role models.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Feminism extended its critique to areas of activity, including science and social science. Which of the following is NOT a feminist critique of science?
options: The term ‘androcentric’ was used to describe this process.
It was conducted to serve humanitarian interest.
Science, in particular, was for much of its history a male activity.
Goals of science: objectivity, explanation and prediction arose from masculine ways of conceiving the world.
explanation: Feminist critiques say science was male-dominated ('androcentric') and its aims of objectivity and prediction came from masculine ways of thinking. The statement that science served purely humanitarian interests is not part of this critique.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: A knowledge of all the subjects cannot be acquired by one person. A person with a basic background in a subject cannot build knowledge. Knowledge can only be developed through:
explanation: Knowledge cannot be fully gained from teaching or research alone. It is built through experience, as people interact with the world and reflect on it.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following is a crucial element in developing a country's curriculum?
explanation: A curriculum is designed to meet the needs of society, so this is the most crucial element. Medium of instruction and teaching methods follow from it.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following approaches is meaningful learning emphasised through interaction in group settings?
explanation: In group discussions, students share and debate ideas with one another, which makes learning meaningful. Quizzes and assignments do not stress interaction as much.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: In a ‘good’ system, all aspects of teaching and assessment are tuned to support high- level learning, so that all students are encouraged to use higher-order learning processes. Constructive alignment (CA) is such a system. It is an approach to curriculum design that optimizes the conditions for quality learning (John Biggs, 2023). The ‘constructive’ aspect refers to the idea that students construct meaning through relevant learning activities. What is the author trying to convey here?
options: The ‘alignment’ aspect refers to what the learner does.
Meaning is not something imparted or transmitted from teacher to learner, but is something learners have to create for themselves.
Teaching does not act simply as a catalyst for learning.
Learners set up an environment that maximises the likelihood that students will engage in the activities designed to achieve the intended outcomes.
explanation: The author says that meaning is not passed from teacher to student. Learners must create meaning for themselves by doing relevant learning activities. This is the idea of constructivism (Biggs).

subject: teaching-methodology
text: When all students are treated equally and given equal opportunities for development, _____________ is ensured.
explanation: Treating everyone equally with equal opportunities is fairness. Equity is different, as it gives more support to those who need it, to reach the same result.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: A teacher intends to use the interdisciplinary curriculum approach for social science pedagogy. Which of the following options would be the most appropriate for her?
options: Grouping of related experiences/events over a specific time span
Relating a concept in social sciences with mathematics/science/astronomy
Designing instructions in consonance with the learners' stages of cognitive development
Identifying local resources for display in class
explanation: The interdisciplinary approach links a concept in one subject with others such as mathematics, science or astronomy. Grouping events by time or by stages of development is a different approach.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: _______ would NOT fall in the category of the Socially Disadvantaged Group.
explanation: Socially disadvantaged groups include migrants, orphans and children in vulnerable situations. Being a student from a village does not make one socially disadvantaged by itself.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: As per NEP 2020, the 'Gender Inclusion Fund' by the Government of India will provide equitable quality education for all ______________.
explanation: NEP 2020 sets up a Gender Inclusion Fund to give equitable, quality education to all girls and transgender students.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following is NOT true about simulation?
options: It is used to teach concepts in a better way.
Facilitators can introduce it based on real events only.
It is an imitation of a real world example.
Facilitators can introduce it based on real and imaginary events.
explanation: A simulation imitates real life, and it can be based on both real and imaginary events. So saying it can be based only on real events is not true.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the symposium technique?
options: The group will not discuss the strategy and sequence to be followed in Symposium.
A large number of students will investigate a theme and then make an oral presentation in a larger gathering of students and teachers.
The group may meet again after the Symposium to discuss the input collected from audience.
Subject teacher or a senior teacher will be the moderator.
explanation: In a symposium the group does plan the strategy and sequence beforehand, so the statement that they will not discuss it is not true. The symposium is where several speakers present views on a theme before an audience, with a moderator.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Teachers are always confronted with the question of how to teach a particular subject and also how to combine _______.
explanation: Teachers must decide how to teach (pedagogy) and what to teach (content), and how the two are combined is called pedagogical content knowledge.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: In which of the following techniques is there a one-to-one meeting between the teacher and the student, in which the student presents the work done on a specific assignment, followed by a question-answer session between the teacher and the student?
explanation: A tutorial is a one-to-one meeting of teacher and student, in which the student presents their work and then answers questions.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Pedagogy is related to which of the following?
explanation: Pedagogy is the art and science of teaching, so it is related to teaching methodology, i.e. how teaching is done.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) of India aims to improve the _______ of people in underdeveloped districts through convergence, collaboration and competition.
explanation: The Aspirational Districts Programme (2018) of NITI Aayog aims to improve the living standards of people in the most underdeveloped districts through convergence, collaboration and competition.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: According to RPWD Act, 2016, 'Inclusive Education' means:
options: a specialised system of education for the students with disability
a system of education wherein students from SEWGs learn together
a system of education wherein students with and without disability learn together
a system of education wherein students from economically weaker sections and students with disability learn together
explanation: As per the RPWD Act 2016, inclusive education is a system in which students with and without disabilities learn together.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Radio talks, academic discussions are examples of:
explanation: A register is the style of language used in a particular situation. Radio talks and academic discussions are in the spoken mode, so they are registers for spoken mode.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Curriculum is the instructional and educational programme through which students achieve their life goals, ideas and aspirations. It is a curriculum through which the general aims of school education are given concrete form. However, there is a major difference between the traditional and modern approaches to the curriculum. Identify the ideal difference between them.
options: The traditional curriculum includes co-curricular activities, whereas the modern curriculum focuses on planned classroom activities.
The traditional curriculum focuses on all aspects related to the students' social environment, whereas the modern curriculum focuses on cognitive dimensions.
In the modern curriculum, everything is centred on adult learners, whereas the traditional curriculum is centred on basic learners.
The traditional curriculum was subject-centred, whereas the modern curriculum is child- and life-centred.
explanation: The traditional curriculum was subject-centred, focusing on books and content. The modern curriculum is child-centred and life-centred, and considers the learner's needs and daily life.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Who was the first Indian educationist and philosopher to acknowledge the importance of art in education?
explanation: Rabindranath Tagore stressed art, music and dance in education and started Santiniketan and Visva-Bharati on this belief.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Observation, hypothesis, testing and formulation are the linguistic characteristics of _______.
explanation: Science uses a language of observation, hypothesis, testing and formulation of laws, which is a specific characteristic of scientific language.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following is NOT a stage of cognitive development, as per Piaget?
explanation: Piaget's four stages are sensorimotor, pre-operational, concrete operational and formal operational. There is no 'post-operational' stage.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: In contrast to the behaviourist perspective of the stimulus-response relationship, learning came to be regarded as an active process. This theory is known as ________.
explanation: Behaviourists saw learning as stimulus and response. Constructivism sees learning as an active process in which learners build knowledge for themselves.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: To realise the vision of NEP 2020, _______ (SEZ) have been established to focus on equity and inclusion.
explanation: NEP 2020 proposes Special Education Zones (SEZs) in disadvantaged regions, with focus on equity and inclusion.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Teaching-learning resources that cannot be easily bought, measured or adjusted are classified as:
explanation: Abstract resources are things like time, motivation and skills of people, which cannot be easily bought, measured or adjusted, unlike physical resources like books.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following is NOT a developmental change, even though they may affect development?
explanation: Development means changes in physical, mental and emotional areas. 'Temporary' is not a type of developmental change, since developmental changes are lasting and gradual.

subject: teaching-methodology
text:
Arrange the general steps of test construction in the correct order.
(a) Writing the items of the test
(b) Planning the test
(c) Preparing the manual for the test and its reproduction
(d) Preparing norms for the final test
explanation: The steps of test construction are: planning the test, writing the items, preparing norms for the final test and preparing the manual and its reproduction.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following dialects is codified and is more likely to be used as a unifying force of the state?
explanation: A standard dialect is the codified form of language taught in schools and used in official work, so it works as a unifying force in a state.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Michael Schneider and Elsbeth Stern consider knowledge acquisition to be the core of the learning process. According to them, which of the following is NOT a cognitive perspective of learning?
options: Learning is not constrained by the capacity limits of human information processing.
Learning is necessarily done by the learner.
Learning requires the integration of knowledge structures.
Optimal learning takes prior knowledge into account.
explanation: In the cognitive perspective, learning is done by the learner, integrates knowledge structures and takes prior knowledge into account. It is limited by the capacity of human information processing, so 'not constrained' is wrong.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: According to the constructivist theory, learners construct their new knowledge on the basis of which of the following?
explanation: According to constructivism, learners construct new knowledge on the basis of their prior experience and understanding.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: A teacher who builds on the learners' prior knowledge, assigns them project work, conducts group activity among students, and provides reinforcement and feedback in the classroom is actually following the _______ paradigm of teaching.
explanation: Building on prior knowledge, giving project work, group activities, and feedback are all constructivist practices, where the learner builds their own knowledge.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following is NOT included in the criteria for assigning duties to existing teachers and selecting new teachers?
explanation: Teachers are chosen and assigned duties on the basis of competence, commitment and professional skills. Body language is not a criterion.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: The processes of thinking, creating, narrating, appreciating, reflecting, experiencing, etc. together constitute ____________.
options: the broad discipline of social science
explanation: Thinking, creating, narrating, appreciating, reflecting and experiencing are the processes that together make up the humanities.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following is NOT the meaning of unit planning and teaching?
explanation: Unit planning uses self-activity, integration and motivation. It is about organising a topic into a meaningful whole, and not the study of traditional methods.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Translanguaging is a characteristic of:
explanation: Translanguaging is when a multilingual person uses all the languages they know freely to communicate and learn. So it is a feature of multilingualism.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: In the psychomotor domain, at the _____ level, an individual demonstrates the ability to reliably aim at a target while throwing a dart.
explanation: In the psychomotor domain, the 'complex overt response' level is when a person performs a skilful act smoothly and reliably, like reliably hitting a dartboard target.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Extensive reading generally occurs when _____.
options: students are alone, such as in a library
students are studying co-curricular subjects in school
explanation: Extensive reading is reading for pleasure and general understanding, generally done alone, e.g. in a library. Intensive reading is detailed reading of short texts in class.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following statements regarding basic pedagogical guidelines is NOT true?
options: The learning environment should promote independence, interdependence and self-motivation
Learning programmes should be according to the teacher
Providing students with a safe, nurturing and productive environment
explanation: Learning programmes should be designed around the needs of learners, not according to what the teacher likes. The other statements are basic guidelines of good pedagogy.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: One of the examples of the affective domain, 'A person's lifestyle influences their responses in a variety of situations', falls under which of the following headings?
explanation: In the affective domain, 'characterisation' is the highest level, where values become part of a person's lifestyle and affect their behaviour in many situations.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: 'Girls keep things organised and tidy, boys are disorganised and dirty.' This statement is an example of _____.
explanation: Assuming that girls are always tidy and boys always messy is a gender stereotype, i.e. a fixed idea about how a gender behaves.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following comes under the category of 'locomotor disability'?
explanation: Locomotor disability is a disability of movement of the limbs. Cerebral palsy affects muscle control and movement, so it is included. Autism is a developmental condition and not a locomotor disability.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: The aesthetic object is an object of _____ experience and is enjoyed as such.
explanation: An aesthetic object, such as a painting or music, is experienced through the senses and enjoyed for its own sake, so it is an object of sensory experience.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: What is meant by integrating drama and art in the school curriculum?
options: Connecting with school subjects and forms of art education
explanation: Integrating drama and art means linking art forms with school subjects, so that students learn concepts through drama, painting and other arts.

subject: teaching-methodology
text:
Match the following columns of changes occurring during adolescence with the corresponding characteristics.
(a) Growth Spurt | (i) Rapid development of reproductive organs indicating sexual maturity.
(b) Puberty | (ii) Critically evaluating one's body and self-image.
(c) Body image and adjustment | (iii) Adolescence presents identity-related tasks that appear to play an important role in making a successful transition to adulthood.
(d) Identity | (iv) Rapid increase in height and weight
explanation: Growth spurt: sudden rise in height and weight. Puberty: reproductive organs mature. Body image: judging one's own body. Identity: the adolescent's task of forming a sense of self.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: In the _____ approach, a reader moves from part to whole in terms of interpretation of words, sentences as well as ideas.
explanation: In the bottom-up approach, a reader starts with small parts (letters, words) and builds up to the meaning of sentences and ideas. Top-down starts from the overall meaning.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following is related to the restructuring of receipts and expenditure to promote gender equality?
explanation: Gender budgeting means planning and restructuring government receipts and expenditure to promote gender equality.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: A curriculum planned by groups outside an educational institution is what type of curriculum?
explanation: A societal curriculum is planned by groups outside the school, such as society, the state and the community. Institutional curriculum is planned by the school.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following is an example of 'descriptive' teaching in which the input is directly provided by the teacher?
explanation: In the lecture method the teacher gives the input directly and explains, and students mostly listen. It is a descriptive method.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: According to Piaget's cognitive development, in which stage does an individual develop abstract and logical thinking?
explanation: In Piaget's formal operational stage (11+ years), a person can think abstractly and logically, and can solve hypothetical problems.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following terms are NOT related to curriculum flexibility?
options: Determination of goals, materials, methods and evaluation procedures by policymakers
explanation: A flexible curriculum gives autonomy to teachers and students, respects diverse learners and encourages a growth mindset. If policymakers decide everything, it is rigid, so that is not related to flexibility.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: In NEP 2020, the Gender Inclusion Fund is for _____.
explanation: NEP 2020 creates the Gender Inclusion Fund for quality education for all girls and transgender persons.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following is NOT a primary area of development?
explanation: The main areas of development are physical, cognitive, emotional and social. 'Situational' is not an area of development.

subject: teaching-methodology
text: Which of the following is NOT an example of a hidden curriculum related to gender sensitivity?
options: Avoiding the use of adjectives such as beautiful, pretty, obedient, polite for girls and brave, courageous, strong, handsome for boys.
Planning theatre or drama to sensitise students to learning to live together.
Involving boys in the school's social service activities.
Using encouraging words such as excellent, good, well done for both boys and girls.
